items.title: Auto session titles silently skipped when history contains technical role='user' entries (compaction, background notifications, image attachments)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
### Summary
Sessions permanently stay untitled when the turn history contains more than 2 `role="user"` messages, because `maybe_auto_title()` counts **all** `role="user"` entries in `conversation_history` as real user input. In gateway/desktop histories, most `role="user"` entries are not user input at all: context-compaction placeholders, background-process notifications, image-attachment descriptions, model-change notices, and retry/replay duplicates. Once any of these appears before the first clean response, the session is never titled — silently, with no log line and no retry.

### Root cause
`agent/title_generator.py`, `maybe_auto_title()`:

```python
# Count user messages in history to detect first exchange.
# conversation_history includes the exchange that just happened,
# so for a first exchange we expect exactly 1 user message
# (or 2 counting system). Be generous: generate on first 2 exchanges.
user_msg_count = sum(1 for m in (conversation_history or []) if m.get("role") == "user")
if user_msg_count > 2:
    return
```

The heuristic assumes `role="user"` == real user turn. That assumption does not hold for gateway/desktop sessions, where system-injected markers are persisted with `role="user"`:

- `[CONTEXT COMPACTION — REFERENCE ONLY] ...` (compaction placeholder)
- `[IMPORTANT: Background process <id> exited (exit code N). Command: ...]` (background-process notifications)
- `[The user attached an image: ...]` (image descriptions)
- replay duplicates of earlier turns after compaction/interruption

### Evidence (local repro, Hermes desktop app on Windows)
- Session A: 11 `role="user"` rows in history, only **3** were real user messages; the rest were the marker types above. Result: no title.
- Session B: 21 `role="user"` rows, ~8 real (including compaction replays of the same message). Result: no title.
- Control: a session whose history had 0 user entries was titled correctly.
- `agent.log` shows no error — the guard returns silently, which is why this is invisible.
- The configured title provider is healthy: a backfill using the same provider and `generate_title()` produced titles immediately for both affected sessions.

### Suggested fix
Replace the message-count heuristic with the DB title as the single source of truth (the session should be titled as long as it has no title yet), plus a process-local in-flight guard so a second worker isn't spawned while one is still running:

```python
# Process-local in-flight guard: prevents a second title-generation call
# for the same session while a background worker is still running.
_title_in_flight: set[str] = set()
_title_in_flight_lock = threading.Lock()

def maybe_auto_title(session_db, session_id, user_message, assistant_response,
                     conversation_history, failure_callback=None, main_runtime=None,
                     title_callback=None, runtime_validator=None) -> None:
    if not session_db or not session_id or not user_message or not assistant_response:
        return
    with _title_in_flight_lock:
        if session_id in _title_in_flight:
            return
        try:
            existing = session_db.get_session_title(session_id)
        except Exception:
            return
        if existing:
            return
        _title_in_flight.add(session_id)
    if not _auto_title_enabled():
        with _title_in_flight_lock:
            _title_in_flight.discard(session_id)
        return

    def _run() -> None:
        try:
            auto_title_session(session_db, session_id, user_message, assistant_response,
                               failure_callback=failure_callback, main_runtime=main_runtime,
                               title_callback=title_callback, runtime_validator=runtime_validator)
        finally:
            with _title_in_flight_lock:
                _title_in_flight.discard(session_id)

    thread = threading.Thread(target=_run, daemon=True, name="auto-title")
    thread.start()
```

`conversation_history` stays in the signature for backward compatibility but is deliberately not used as a first-exchange heuristic.

### Impact
Affects any session (desktop and gateway) whose first clean response arrives after compaction, a background-process notification, an image attachment, or an interruption that replays earlier turns — i.e. most non-trivial first exchanges in long-lived desktop sessions. Users simply see sessions without titles; no error is surfaced.

### Tests
`tests/agent/test_title_generator.py`: 17 tests pass with the suggested change (two tests updated from the count-heuristic semantics: one asserting a session with an existing title is skipped, one asserting no double-fire while a worker is in flight).

items.body:
### Bug Description

On every start of Hermes Desktop, a Windows WebAuthn dialog appears ("Choose a passkey — Passkey for google.com"). The Google session is never remembered, so a full re-login is requested each launch. Still present after upgrading to v0.19.1.

Two network storage locations, neither of which appears to persist cookies for the embedded session:

1. `%APPDATA%\Hermes\Partitions\hermes-embed\Network` — no `Cookies` file at all. Contains only Network Persistent State, NetworkDataMigrated, Trust Tokens, Trust Tokens-journal. The partition is actively written to (folder modified 2026-08-02 08:22), so it is not a stale leftover.

2. `%APPDATA%\Hermes\Network` — a `Cookies` file exists but is dated 2026-06-04 16:04, while `Network Persistent State` in the same folder was modified 2026-08-02 13:12. The cookie store has not been written to in roughly two months, including across the v0.19.1 upgrade.

My interpretation: the embedded session hosting the Google login has no persistent cookie storage, so each launch presents itself to Google as an unrecognised client.

Note: disabling the `google-oauth-setup` and `google-workspace` skills does not stop the prompt, consistent with the connection being established by the app itself at startup rather than by a skill.

### Steps to Reproduce

A full Google login is requested on every start. Clicking Cancel is harmless — Calendar continues to work normally afterwards.

### Expected Behavior

The session is remembered and no re-authentication is requested on subsequent starts.

### Actual Behavior

A full Google login is requested on every start. Clicking Cancel is harmless — Calendar continues to work normally afterwards.

items.title: [Bug]: Model switch mid-session triggers history_version mismatch — all subsequent agent output discarded (empty assistant messages in DB)

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug Description

When a model switch occurs mid-session (via system-injected `[System: The active model for this chat has changed to...]` message), the `history_version` guard in `server.py:9548-9571` discards all subsequent agent output, producing empty assistant messages in the session DB.

### Root Cause

`server.py:9192` snapshots `history_version` at turn start. During the turn, the model-switch path (or a side-effect of the injected system message) increments `session["history_version"]`. When the turn completes at line 9548, `current_version != history_version`, so the defensive backstop fires:

```python
# server.py:9548-9571
with session["history_lock"]:
    current_version = int(session.get("history_version", 0))
    if current_version == history_version:
        session["history"] = result["messages"]
        session["history_version"] = history_version + 1
    else:
        # History mutated externally during the turn
        print(
            f"[tui_gateway] prompt.submit: history_version mismatch "
            f"(expected={history_version} current={current_version}) — "
            f"agent output NOT written to session history",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
```

The code comment acknowledges this is a known gap: *"History mutated externally during the turn (undo/compress/retry/rollback now guard on session.running, but this is the defensive backstop for any path that slips past)."* The model-switch path slips past this guard.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a session with any model
2. Send a message — assistant responds normally (verified in DB: content-length > 0)
3. Switch models mid-session (e.g. via `/model` or provider-side model change that injects `[System: The active model for this chat has changed to...]`)
4. Send another message — assistant responds in TUI (WebSocket stream), but DB stores empty content (length=0)
5. All subsequent turns produce empty assistant messages in DB

### Observed Behavior

- **TUI**: Responses appear normally (rendered from WebSocket stream, not DB)
- **Session DB** (`state.db`): Assistant messages have `content=""` (length 0)
- **session_search()**: Returns empty assistant messages — unusable
- **/rewind, /undo**: Operate on corrupted history
- **Cron context_from**: Injects empty history
- **Container log**: `[tui_gateway] prompt.submit: history_version mismatch (expected=1 current=2) — agent output NOT written to session history`

### Evidence

Reproduced on Hermes in Docker (s6-supervised), profile `default`, model switch from `minimax-m3` to `deepseek-v4-pro` via ollama-cloud provider.

Session `20260802_151208_b9d649` in `state.db`:
- 7 user messages, 156 total messages
- First assistant response (before model switch): 1,533 chars ✓
- All 75+ subsequent assistant responses: 0 chars ✗
- 33 empty assistant messages deleted manually to clean up

### Expected Behavior

Model switch should either:
1. Not mutate `history_version` during an in-flight turn, OR
2. The turn completion guard should accept the output even when version changed (the output is still valid — it was produced for the correct history snapshot)

### Impact

- Session history corruption — silent data loss
- Breaks session_search, /rewind, /undo, cron context_from
- User sees responses in TUI but can't search/resume/replay them

### Workaround

Run `/new` before switching models to start a fresh session.

### Related Issues

- #66429: Empty assistant messages (different root cause — messages *sent* empty, not *discarded*)
- #73680: Model changes from other instances corrupting sessions (different mechanism)
- #70516: Stale truncate_before_user_ordinal (closed, related history_version guard)

### Environment

- Hermes in Docker (s6-overlay)
- Profile: default
- Provider: ollama-cloud
- Models: minimax-m3 → deepseek-v4-pro
- `state.db` at `/opt/data/state.db`

items.title: read_file reports valid UTF-8 text as binary when the 1000-byte sample cuts a multibyte character (regression in 0.19.1)
items.body:
I updated the agent image this morning and a couple of my Obsidian notes stopped opening — `read_file` returns "Binary file - cannot display as text" for them. They're plain UTF-8 markdown and they read fine before the update.

Turned out it isn't the files. `read_file` samples with `head -c 1000`, and the terminal layer decodes stdout with `errors="replace"`, so when byte 1000 lands in the middle of a multibyte character the sample picks up a U+FFFD that the file never contained. `_is_likely_binary` then rejects the file on the strength of that character alone.

In the image I'm running (revision `927662e`): the check is at `tools/file_operations.py:896`, the sample is taken at `:1134`, and `read_file_raw` does the same thing at `:1252`.

Most of my notes are Turkish, so ç/ğ/ı/ö/ş/ü are everywhere. 2 of the 171 files in my workspace happened to land on the boundary. Both are valid UTF-8 from start to finish.

Repro, no dependencies:

```sh
printf 'a%.0s' $(seq 999) > fails.md && printf '\303\247\nx\n' >> fails.md   # 'ç' starts at byte 1000
printf 'a%.0s' $(seq 998) > ok.md    && printf '\303\247\nx\n' >> ok.md      # 'ç' fits inside the sample
```

`read_file fails.md` → `is_binary: true`. `read_file ok.md` → reads normally. Same content, same encoding, one byte of offset between them.

This is new in 0.19.1. I still had the 0.19.0 image around and ran the same file through both:

| version | fails.md |
| --- | --- |
| 0.19.0 | reads fine |
| 0.19.1 | "Binary file - cannot display as text" |

`_is_likely_binary` in 0.19.0 has no U+FFFD check at all — just the extension list and the non-printable ratio. The rest of the function is unchanged between the two.

One more thing that might help narrow it down: `patch` edits these same files without complaining. Only `read` refuses them, so the classification isn't shared across the file tools.

Environment: hermes-agent 0.19.1 (`nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest`, image `2e84330df401`), Docker on Windows 11, desktop app 40.10.2. Happy to test a patch against my workspace if that helps.

items.title: [Bug]: [Windows] Dragging any file into Desktop chat throws WinError 5 (terminal.cwd relative path resolves to System32)

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
### Bug Description

Dragging **any** file (PDF, XLSX, TXT, etc.) into the Hermes Desktop chat composer immediately shows an error toast: `[WinError 5] 拒绝访问。: 'C:\Windows\System32\.hermes'` (WinError 5 = Access denied).

This is **not** file-specific — it happens with every file, including plain text files on the Desktop. The reported path (`C:\Windows\System32\.hermes`) is the smoking gun: Hermes tries to create a `.hermes` directory **relative to the process CWD**, which is `C:\Windows\System32` for the desktop app on this machine. `System32` is a protected directory, so the `mkdir` fails with WinError 5.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Windows 11 machine, Hermes Desktop app v0.19.1 (2026.7.30).
2. Ensure `config.yaml` has `terminal.cwd: .` (the default, per `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:241`).
3. Launch Hermes Desktop such that its process CWD is `C:\Windows\System32` (reproduced in this environment).
4. Drag any file (PDF / XLSX / TXT) into the chat composer.
5. Observe the error toast: `[WinError 5] 拒绝访问。: 'C:\Windows\System32\.hermes'`.

Direct reproduction of the failing operation:
```bash
cd C:\Windows\System32
python -c "import os; os.makedirs(r'C:\Windows\System32\.hermes_test')"
# -> PermissionError: [WinError 5] 拒绝访问。: 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\.hermes_test'
```

### Expected Behavior

The attachment/file pipeline should resolve paths against **HERMES_HOME** (absolute, e.g. `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes` or `~/.hermes`), never against the process CWD — or at minimum, a relative `cwd: .` should be resolved safely to the user's home when the process CWD is not writable. A relative `terminal.cwd` should not silently resolve to a protected system directory like `C:\Windows\System32`.

### Actual Behavior

Dragging any file into the Desktop composer throws `[WinError 5] 拒绝访问。: 'C:\Windows\System32\.hermes'`; the toast is opaque (no hint about CWD), and all file attachments are unusable until the config is fixed manually. The failure surfaces in the drag-and-drop attachment pipeline (`eagerlyUploadAttachment` → `readFileDataUrlForAttach`), but the underlying broken path affects any file operation that resolves relative to CWD.

Workaround (confirmed to fix it):
```bash
hermes config set terminal.cwd "C:\Users\cheny"
```
then restart the desktop app / gateway.

### Affected Component

Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
Debug report (local, not uploaded — contains personal info):
- version: 0.19.1 [0a62610f] (2026-08-02)
- os: Windows 10 AMD64
- python: 3.11.15
- profile: default
- hermes_home: ~/AppData\Local\hermes
- terminal: local
- gateway: running (pid 14500)
```

### Operating System

Windows 11 25H2 (Build 26200)

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.19.1 (2026.7.30), upstream 26e0b1c1

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`terminal.cwd` in `config.yaml` is set to **`.` (a relative path)**:

```yaml
terminal:
  backend: local
  modal_mode: auto
  cwd: .        # <-- relative path
```

1. The default value in `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:241` is `"cwd": "."` ("Use current directory").
2. `agent/runtime_cwd.py:73` (`resolve_agent_cwd()`) falls back to `Path(os.getcwd())` when the configured cwd is relative/unresolvable.
3. When the Electron desktop app is launched from a context whose process CWD is `C:\Windows\System32` (common for GUI apps started from certain shells, Task Scheduler, or admin contexts), every cwd-relative path resolves to `C:\Windows\System32\...`.
4. Code paths that `mkdir('.hermes')` / `mkdir(<cwd>/.hermes)` then fail with `[WinError 5] 拒绝访问` because `C:\Windows\System32` is not writable by a normal (non-elevated) user.
5. The failure surfaces in the drag-and-drop attachment pipeline (`eagerlyUploadAttachment` → `readFileDataUrlForAttach`), but the underlying broken path affects any file operation that resolves relative to CWD.

Also observed: an old `.env` had `# TERMINAL_CWD=.` commented out — the migration from `TERMINAL_CWD` (absolute `C:\Users\cheny`) to `terminal.cwd` in config.yaml produced a **relative** `.` value, losing the original absolute home path.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

1. **Change the default** in `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:241` from `"cwd": "."` to an absolute default (e.g. `str(Path.home())`), matching what `hermes_cli/setup.py:1376` already does (`config["terminal"].setdefault("cwd", str(Path.home()))`).
2. **Harden `resolve_agent_cwd()`** (`agent/runtime_cwd.py:60-73`): when the resolved cwd is not writable (e.g. `os.access(p, os.W_OK)` fails) or is a system-protected directory (e.g. under `C:\Windows\System32`), fall back to `Path.home()` instead of `os.getcwd()`.
3. **Config migration**: when migrating legacy `TERMINAL_CWD` → `terminal.cwd`, preserve the absolute value instead of defaulting to `.`.

Verification: `hermes config set terminal.cwd "C:\Users\cheny"` resolves the issue; dragging files into the composer works again.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: Desktop: pin/unpin still reverted by a list page that lands after the PATCH ack (follow-up to #74570)

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

items.body:
## Bug

After the #74570 fix (`090d14647`), a fresh local pin/unpin is protected **while the PATCH is in flight** (`unconfirmed` guard). But the guard is cleared on the PATCH's own ack, and a **session-list request issued before the write can land after the ack** still carrying the pre-write value. The pull pass then reads that stale row with no guard left and reverts the user's action — and because the reverted state is pushed back to the server by the next reconcile, the wrong value becomes durable.

User-visible symptom: pin/unpin works **intermittently** — clicking "unpin" in the sidebar sometimes sticks, sometimes instantly reverts and the session stays pinned (the server row is re-PATCHed back to `pinned=true` by the resurrection).

## Timeline (unpin example)

```
t-1  list request #N issued (server row still pinned=true)     <- stale page in flight
t0   user unpins -> reconcile -> PATCH pinned=false issued     <- unconfirmed.set(id, false)
t1   PATCH ack -> unconfirmed.delete(id)                       <- guard gone (090d14647 clears on ack)
t2   list response #N lands (pinned=true) -> $sessions change -> reconcile -> pullRemotePins()
     -> no pending, no unconfirmed -> row.pinned && !heldLocally -> pinSession() -> PIN RESURRECTED
t3   resurrection fires reconcile -> PATCH pinned=true -> server row flipped back
```

The symmetric race hits pin too (stale `pinned=false` page after a pin's ack -> `unpinSession()`).

Why the ack is not enough: the `unconfirmed` guard's lifetime is the PATCH request itself, but the stale list page's lifetime can be longer — list requests are heavier and slower, and `refreshSessions()` runs on every `message.complete`/turn/focus, so the window is real and recurring.

## Evidence

- `pullRemotePins()` in `apps/desktop/src/store/session-pin-sync.ts` (current main): `unconfirmed` is deleted in `writePin()`'s `.then()` — the pull pass can no longer distinguish "page issued before the write" from "genuinely newer truth" once the ack landed.
- The existing test `ignores a stale page that contradicts a write still in flight` only covers a stale page arriving **before** the ack; the post-ack window is untested. Its final assertion ("once acked, later server truth is honoured") assumes every post-ack page is new — not true for requests issued pre-write.
- Reproduced in practice on macOS (Desktop 0.17.0 build containing `090d14647`): a just-unpinned session reappears pinned in the sidebar and `sessions.pinned` in state.db reads back `1`.

## Suggested fix

Keep the write guard until a list page **confirms the written value**, with a cooldown fallback so it can't go stale forever:

- `writePin()`: record `{ value, at: Date.now() }` and do NOT clear on ack.
- `pullRemotePins()`: if a guard exists for the row and `guard.value !== row.pinned` **and** `Date.now() - guard.at < COOLDOWN_MS` (e.g. 5s), skip the row (stale page). Otherwise delete the guard and reconcile normally — the page confirms the write, or is old enough that it must be fresh truth.
- A failed PATCH still clears the guard so later pages are honoured.

This preserves the cross-app sync (a genuinely newer page from another app is adopted) while closing the post-ack stale-page window. I have a working patch + regression tests (pin and unpin directions, guard confirmation, cooldown expiry) ready to open as a PR if this approach is accepted.

## Environment

- Hermes Desktop 0.17.0 (build containing `090d14647`), Hermes Agent v0.19.x, macOS 27.0 (arm64)
- Upstream main @ `4983c576b` — `apps/desktop/src/store/session-pin-sync.ts` unchanged since `090d14647`

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop remote mode — non-image MEDIA files (.xlsx, .pdf, .csv) show 'missing, unreadable, or too large' on click
items.body:
## Bug Description

In **remote-gateway mode** (Hermes Desktop on laptop → Hermes Gateway on VPS), `MEDIA:` tokens for **non-image files** (`.xlsx`, `.pdf`, `.csv`, `.docx`, etc.) render as clickable links in chat, but clicking them shows **"Couldn't fetch {filename} from the gateway (missing, unreadable, or too large)."** The file exists on the gateway, is valid, and is well under any size cap.

Images (`.png`, `.jpg`) work correctly — the bug is specific to **non-image file types**.

## Root Cause (from source analysis)

In `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/markdown-text.tsx`, the `MediaAttachment` component:

```tsx
if (kind === 'file') {
    setFailed(true)   // ← .xlsx → mediaKind() returns 'file' → immediate failure
    return             // ← never attempts downloadGatewayMediaFile()
}
```

`mediaKind('.xlsx')` returns `'file\` (not `'image'`/`'audio'`/`'video'`) → the component sets `failed = true` immediately without attempting any fetch. The fallback click handler calls `downloadGatewayMediaFile()` → `/api/fs/read-data-url`, which is data-URL capped and can fail for legitimate files.

This is the same class of bug as #44523 (closed in v2026.7.7), but that fix only covered **images** and **audio/video**. **Non-image generic files** still hit the dead-end path.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Hermes Desktop (v0.19.1 / v2026.7.30) connected to a **remote gateway** (VPS over network).
2. Ask the agent to read or generate a `.xlsx` file (e.g. a spreadsheet the agent creates on the gateway).
3. Agent returns a `MEDIA:/path/to/file.xlsx` token.
4. Chat renders: `Open Anexa_2_Calculator_RFP_IT.xlsx` link.
5. Click the link → **"Couldn't fetch Anexa_2_Calculator_RFP_IT.xlsx from the gateway (missing, unreadable, or too large)."**
6. File is confirmed valid on the gateway: 8.8 KB, `Microsoft Excel 2007+`, readable via `openpyxl`.

## Expected Behavior

Non-image files should download via the authenticated filesystem bridge (native save dialog), same as the fix proposed in PR #63808.

## Actual Behavior

`MediaAttachment` sets `failed = true` for `kind === 'file'` without attempting fetch. The error message is misleading — the file is not missing, unreadable, or too large.

## Environment

- **Backend (VPS):** Hermes Agent v0.19.1 (v2026.7.30), upstream `ec4f8419`, Python 3.11.15, Linux (Ubuntu), `hermes dashboard` on port 9119 with auth.
- **Client (laptop):** Hermes Desktop v0.19.1, remote-gateway mode.

items.title: [Bug]: Background review fork doesn't receive the WebUI gateway's per-request system-prompt injection → prompt-cache miss on every review

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P0
labels.description: Critical — data loss, security, crash loop

labels.name: sweeper:risk-caching
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break/degrade prompt caching or cache-key stability (invariant)

items.body:
## Summary

The background memory/skill review fork builds its request from the agent's cached system prompt, but the WebUI gateway injects a **"WebUI session context"** block into the system prompt of every main-chat request. The fork's requests therefore diverge from the parent's cached prompt exactly where that section begins (~31K tokens in), so the fork can **never append to the parent's KV/prefix cache**.

- On single-slot local llama.cpp: a **93K-token full re-prefill (~4 min on an R9700) every ~10 turns**.
- On cloud providers: silently ~28K tokens of prefill per review run + a ~345K cold first run per session.

This contradicts the design intent in `agent/background_review.py` ("the fork inherits the parent's live runtime... so it hits the same prefix cache").

## Root cause (byte-level evidence, `--log-prompts-dir`)

The fork's rendered prompt is **byte-identical to the parent's last request for the first 94,274 bytes**, then:

```
parent @ 94,274:  ...Provider: custom
                   Platform: webui

                   WebUI session context:
                   - This browser session is not the same live transcript as Telegram, Disc...

fork   @ 94,274:  ...Provider: custom
                   Platform: webui<|im_end|>
                   <|im_start|>user
                   And us side often offer no help?...
```

Section presence across consecutive prompt dumps:

| Dump | Request | "WebUI session context" | "Connected Platforms" |
|---|---|---|---|
| 000000741922 | parent (in-turn) | 1× | 1× |
| 000000747029 | parent's last request | 1× | 1× |
| 000000766505 | **review fork, 1st call** | **0×** | **0×** |
| 000000815661 | review fork, 2nd call | 0× | 0× |
| 000000862537 | review fork, 3rd call | 0× | 0× |

The missing block is a **3,101-char gateway-injected section**: session ID, workspace, WebUI progress guidance, connected platforms, and scheduled-task delivery options.

Code path: `_run_review_in_thread` pins `review_agent._cached_system_prompt = agent._cached_system_prompt` (`background_review.py`), but the gateway's per-request system-prompt injection (the WebUI session-context block) is applied on top of the cached prompt for main-chat requests only — there is no path for it to reach the fork.

## Impact

| Backend | With section (intended) | Without it (actual) |
|---|---|---|
| Cloud (content-addressed cache) | ~2.5K tokens pp per review | ~28.6K tokens pp per review + one ~345K cold first run |
| Local llama.cpp (single slot) | ~2.5K tokens pp per review | f_keep 0.246–0.648 → full 93K rebuild per review (~240s GPU stall, blocks the user's next request in the queue) |

On local, the 0.25 f_keep discard guard (llama.cpp #26198 / #22746) additionally throws away even the salvageable prefix. The main conversation survives on local only via RAM-cache checkpoint restore of its own entry.

## Reproduction

1. Run the WebUI gateway with a local llama.cpp custom provider; add `--log-prompts-dir <dir>` to llama-server.
2. Use ~10+ turns (any tools).
3. When the background review fires (~10-turn nudge), check llama-server:
   - `f_keep` collapses to ≈0.25–0.65 and prompt processing = the full prompt.
   - Diff the last two prompt dumps — divergence exactly at the "WebUI session context" section start; fork dumps lack the section entirely.

## Suggested fix

- Build the review fork's request through the same per-request assembly as the parent (carry the gateway's system-prompt injection), or
- Have the fork reuse the parent's **last-sent request bytes** (system prompt included) instead of only the cached system prompt.

## Environment

- Hermes 0.19.1 (agent_client_protocol 0.9.0), WebUI gateway
- Custom provider → llama.cpp (Qwen3.6-27B), Vulkan on R9700 (RDNA4), `--cache-ram` + `--ctx-checkpoints`, `--log-prompts-dir`

## Bug Description

The config key `auxiliary.web_extract` is documented in `cli-config.yaml.example` (line 618-622) with the comment:

> ```yaml
> # Web page scraping / summarization + browser page text extraction
> web_extract:

However, no code path in the codebase passes `task="web_extract"` to the auxiliary client, meaning this config is never read or used.

## Investigation

Searched the entire codebase for `task="web_extract"` and `task='web_extract'` — zero results.

The `web_extract_tool` in `tools/web_tools.py` (line 750-751) explicitly states:

> "Returns clean page content (markdown/text) with NO LLM summarization."

The Firecrawl provider's `extract()` method in `plugins/web/firecrawl/provider.py` also does not reference any auxiliary model — it just calls the Firecrawl SDK's `scrape()` and returns raw markdown.

Users who configure `auxiliary.web_extract` with a specific provider/model (as I did below) will see no effect — the config is silently ignored:

```yaml
auxiliary:
  web_extract:
    provider: custom:router
    model: some-model
    timeout: 6000
```

## Expected Behavior

Either:
1. Remove the config key if it's unused, or
2. Wire it up to actually be used (e.g. for LLM-based summarization of extracted content, or for browser page text extraction as the comment suggests)

- Hermes Agent version: latest (main branch as of 2026-08-03)

items.title: Desktop (Electron) freezes / V8 OOM on Linux: backend-restart crash loop + serve-process leak

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Environment
- Hermes Agent v0.19.1 (2026.7.30), upstream 710b0266, local ee276a79
- Linux Mint 22.3 (Ubuntu-based), Cinnamon, LightDM, X11
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX 2070 (proprietary driver)
- RAM 31 GB; sandbox backend switched Modal -> Local
- Host: linuxalmi @ LinuxMaschine

## Symptom
Hermes Desktop (Electron) freezes permanently within seconds of launch.

`~/.hermes/logs/desktop.log` shows a repeating boot crash loop:
```
[hermes] [renderer] webContents became unresponsive
[hermes] [boot] Starting Hermes backend ... HERMES_BACKEND_READY port=XXXXX
[hermes] [boot] Resolving Hermes backend / runtime is ready
  -> boot sequence restarts from the top, spawning a NEW `hermes serve`
```
Up to 12 concurrent `hermes_cli.main serve` processes accumulate, and the
V8 heap grows to ~4000 MB until:
```
V8 javascript OOM (Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit)
[1:...] Mark-Compact 3992.5 (4002.0) -> 3992.5 (4001.8) MB
```

## Root cause (observed)
The renderer goes unresponsive; the boot resolver then tears down and
restarts the backend, which restarts the entire boot sequence in a loop.
Each iteration spawns another `serve` process and leaks V8 heap until OOM.
This is NOT a GPU issue: `HERMES_DESKTOP_DISABLE_GPU=1` was set in
~/.bashrc (and the log confirms GPU was disabled) but the loop persisted
when the desktop was launched via the GUI/menu (env var not inherited).

## Workaround (confirmed working)
Use `hermes dashboard` (browser UI) instead of the Electron desktop.
No Electron, no GPU, no V8-OOM loop. Runs cleanly at http://127.0.0.1:9119.

## Suggested fixes
- Don't restart the whole boot sequence when the renderer is briefly
  unresponsive; add a retry/backoff cap and reuse the existing `serve`.
- Track spawned `serve` processes and reap them on backend restart
  (processes.json showed 0 tracked while 12 were alive).
- Apply HERMES_DESKTOP_DISABLE_GPU / other env overrides regardless of how
  the desktop is launched (GUI vs terminal).

items.title: openai-codex saves smeared progressive preview frames as finished GPT Image 2 images
items.body:
## User-visible failure

On the **openai-codex / GPT Image 2** path, Hermes can return `success: true` and write a PNG that is only an SSE **progressive preview** (`partial_image_b64`). Those frames look smeared, motion-blurred, or unfinished. They are then cached and delivered as finished images.

This is a **stream-handling bug**, not a prompt-quality problem. A completed generate can persist a preview as the production artifact.

Still present on current `main` as of 2026-08-14:

- request still sends `"partial_images": 1`
- `_extract_image_b64` still assigns `found = partial` after a final `result`
- `_collect_image_b64` still keeps last-found bytes and treats any b64 as success

The **P3 / cosmetic** label is wrong for this class of bug.

## Provider path

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Config | `image_gen.provider = openai-codex` |
| Model | `gpt-image-2-high` (also medium/low) |
| Transport | `POST https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses` (SSE) |
| Hosted tool | `image_generation` / `gpt-image-2` |
| Not this path | Direct OpenAI `images.generate` REST |

## Reproduction

1. `image_gen.provider=openai-codex`, `image_gen.model=gpt-image-2-high`
2. Call `image_generate` repeatedly (any prompt — do not branch on content)
3. When a smeared output appears, inspect the SSE stream: often only `partial_image_b64`, no final `item.result`
4. Hermes still returned success and wrote `$HERMES_HOME/cache/images/openai_codex_*`

## Root cause

Two defects:

1. Request layer asks for previews: `"partial_images": 1`
2. Extractor / collector treat any image bytes as the deliverable. A partial can overwrite a coexisting final in the same payload. A partial-only stream is saved as success.

Pixel dimensions are **not** a reliable discriminator. Codex often ignores requested `size`. Gate on `image_source`.

## Fix

Implemented in PR #76967:

- Request `partial_images: 0`
- Track final vs partial separately; final never overwritten by partial
- Deliver only `source=final`; partial-only → `incomplete_image`; empty/non-final → one content-agnostic retry, then fail closed
- Surface `image_source` / `pixel_size` for QA

## Files

- `plugins/image_gen/openai-codex/__init__.py`
- `tests/plugins/image_gen/test_openai_codex_provider.py`

items.title: feat(delegation): survive or report background delegations lost on restart

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Problem
Background `delegate_task` children are silently discarded when the Hermes
process restarts (upgrade, unit restart, crash). The parent session only
learns about it when the user notices the missing result — no summary,
no error, empty transcript dir.

Concrete repro from our setup (desktop-remote, agent on a VM behind
systemd units, build v2026.7.30-583-g9b50a99b3):
1. Parent session dispatches a background delegate_task (~10 min review).
2. `hermes update` restarts the gateway/dashboard units mid-run.
3. The delegation vanishes without a trace; the parent keeps assuming
   a result will arrive.

## Why it matters
Upgrades and restarts are routine; long background tasks are exactly the
ones likely to straddle them. Silent loss is the worst outcome: the
parent cannot distinguish "still running" from "dead".

## Ideas (any of them helps)
- Minimal: on next start, mark in-flight delegations as lost-on-restart
  and deliver a synthetic failure result to the parent session, so it
  can re-dispatch.
- Better: persist the delegation prompt + role + context (not the full
  transcript) and offer resume/re-dispatch on boot.
- Full: checkpoint child state for true resume.

Related: #76605 (results lost under retention prune), #74609 (stop
session background delegations on stop) — this request is the
restart/crash counterpart.

items.title: [Bug]: Bootstrap install fails at "desktop" stage — Node check is a false positive when a stray node symlink has no matching npm (macOS)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
### Bug Description

Fresh CLI install (via the `hermes-agent.nousresearch.com` bootstrap downloader) fails every time at the `desktop` stage with `exit code 1`. The `node-deps` stage also silently degrades — browser-tool and TUI npm installs fail — even though the `prerequisites` stage reports `✓ Node.js v22.22.2 found`. This is a false positive: `npm` is not actually reachable, only `node` is, via a stray symlink (details below).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. On macOS, have a leftover Node symlink on the system PATH that resolves `node` but has no matching `npm` next to it, e.g.:
   ```
   $ ls -la /usr/local/bin/node
   lrwxr-xr-x 1 root wheel 24 Mar 29 2024 /usr/local/bin/node -> /Users/<user>/.n/bin/node
   $ ls -la /usr/local/bin/npm
   ls: /usr/local/bin/npm: No such file or directory
   ```
   (This can happen from any old Node version manager setup — in my case leftover from [`n`](https://github.com/tj/n) — where only `node` ever got globally symlinked.)
2. Have your real, complete Node installs (with matching npm) only reachable via PATH entries set in `~/.zshrc` (e.g. `n`'s `$N_PREFIX/bin`, or Homebrew) rather than `~/.zprofile` or system-wide.
3. Run the bootstrap installer from `hermes-agent.nousresearch.com`.
4. It clones the repo, sets up the venv, installs Python deps — then fails at `node-deps` (`npm: command not found`, silently swallowed) and fatally at `desktop`:
   ```
   ✓ Node.js v22.22.2 found                                          stage=prerequisites
   ...
   stderr: .../install-main.sh: line 2115: npm: command not found    stage=node-deps
   ⚠ npm install failed or timed out (browser tools may not work)    stage=node-deps
   ✓ Node.js dependencies installed                                  stage=node-deps
   ...
   ✓ Node.js v22.22.2 found                                          stage=desktop
   ✗ Cannot build desktop app: Node.js / npm unavailable              stage=desktop
   {"ok":false,"stage":"desktop","skipped":false,"reason":"exit code 1"}
   ERROR hermes_bootstrap_lib::bootstrap: bootstrap FAILED stage=Some("desktop") error=exit code 1
   ```
5. Retrying the install reproduces the identical failure (confirmed twice in a row in my `~/.hermes/logs/bootstrap-installer.log`).

### Expected Behavior

The installer should not report `✓ Node.js found` unless a working `npm` is confirmed alongside it. If a `node` binary resolves but `npm` doesn't, it should be treated the same as "Node not found" and fall through to whatever remediation applies there (probing other known install locations, prompting, etc.), instead of proceeding and failing later at the `desktop` stage. The `node-deps` stage should also not report `✓ Node.js dependencies installed` when the `npm install` calls inside it actually failed.

### Actual Behavior

`install.sh` runs via plain `sh` (`kind=Sh` in the bootstrap log), so it never sources `~/.zshrc`/`~/.zprofile` — it only gets whatever minimal PATH its parent process (the downloader) has. In my environment that resolves to:

```
PATH=/usr/gnu/bin:/usr/local/bin:/bin:/usr/bin:.
```

`/usr/local/bin` contains a stray, root-owned `node` symlink (`-> ~/.n/bin/node`) with no sibling `npm`/`npx`. Whatever check backs "Checking Node.js..." only does `command -v node` (or similar), which succeeds via that stray symlink — so the installer reports Node as found and never looks at my actual complete Node installs (`~/.n/bin`, Homebrew), which are only on PATH via `~/.zshrc`. Every later `npm install`/`npm run pack` call then fails with `npm: command not found`, and the `desktop` stage fails fatally with `exit code 1`.

This confirmed working after manually symlinking npm/npx next to the existing node symlink and retrying (see Proposed Fix / workaround below) — the install then completed successfully.

### Affected Component

Setup / Installation

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

N/A — `hermes debug share` isn't available; the install never completed successfully on the first two attempts (failed at the `desktop` stage both times), so the `hermes` CLI wasn't usable yet. Relevant raw log excerpts from `~/.hermes/logs/bootstrap-installer.log` are included above and in Additional Logs below.

### Operating System

macOS (Darwin 25.6.0), Apple Silicon

### Python Version

3.11.8

### Hermes Version

0.19.1 (installed via fallback tier after `uv.lock` sync also failed — separate issue, see note below)

### Additional Logs / Traceback

```
2026-08-02T18:09:39.889446Z  INFO bootstrap.log: ✗ Cannot build desktop app: Node.js / npm unavailable stage=desktop
2026-08-02T18:09:39.889471Z  INFO bootstrap.log: → Install Node.js and retry: cd /Users/ayush/.hermes/hermes-agent/apps/desktop && npm run pack stage=desktop
2026-08-02T18:09:39.892903Z  INFO bootstrap.log: {"ok":false,"stage":"desktop","skipped":false,"reason":"exit code 1"} stage=desktop
2026-08-02T18:09:39.893186Z ERROR hermes_bootstrap_lib::bootstrap: bootstrap FAILED stage=Some("desktop") error=exit code 1
```

Reproduction of the false-positive Node check in isolation:
```
$ env -i HOME=$HOME sh -c 'command -v node; command -v npm; node -v'
/usr/local/bin/node
v22.22.2
# npm: no output — not found
```

Separately, both install attempts also logged (non-fatal, but worth flagging):
```
stderr: error: The lockfile at `uv.lock` needs to be updated, but `--locked` was provided.
hint: To update the lockfile, run `uv lock`.
⚠ uv.lock sync failed (see uv output above), falling back to PyPI resolve...
⚠ Note: installed via fallback tier (all).
```

### Root Cause Analysis

The Node check (backing "Checking Node.js..." in `install.sh`, invoked with `kind=Sh` / plain `sh`) only verifies `command -v node` succeeds; it never confirms a corresponding `npm` is resolvable from the same PATH. Because `install.sh` runs as a non-login, non-interactive shell, it inherits a minimal PATH rather than the user's `~/.zshrc`-configured one, so it's especially likely to hit a stray/incomplete `node`-only symlink (as here) instead of a complete Node install. The `node-deps` stage compounds this by logging `✓ Node.js dependencies installed` unconditionally even though the `npm install` calls inside that stage already failed (`npm: command not found`), masking the problem until the fatal `desktop` stage.

This is the mirror image of #63612 (false-*negative* Node detection under launchd's empty PATH, followed by the installer clobbering the user's real node/npm/npx) and adjacent to #72073 (`npm not found on PATH` on macOS, but in the Electron update/rebuild path rather than initial install) — same underlying class of bug (installer PATH assumptions around Node/npm), different trigger and failure point.

### Proposed Fix

- In the Node check, don't report success on `command -v node` alone — also require `command -v npm` (ideally verifying both resolve under the same install prefix) before declaring `✓ Node.js found`.
- If `npm` is missing next to an otherwise-valid `node`, treat it like "Node not found" and fall through to the same remediation/discovery logic already used for that case (e.g. probing `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `~/.n/bin`, volta/nvm shims, per the `_discover_homebrew_node_dirs()` precedent referenced in #63612), rather than trusting the first `node` found on a minimal PATH.
- Make the `node-deps` stage's success/failure reporting reflect whether its internal `npm install` calls actually succeeded, instead of unconditionally logging success.

Workaround that resolved it for me — symlink `npm`/`npx` next to the existing stray `node` symlink, then retry the install:
```sh
sudo ln -sf /Users/<user>/.n/bin/npm /usr/local/bin/npm
sudo ln -sf /Users/<user>/.n/bin/npx /usr/local/bin/npx
```
Confirmed: after running this, retrying the bootstrap install completed successfully all the way through.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: Remote mode: projects.* RPCs are not profile-scoped (sidebar shows launch profile's projects)

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
## Summary

In app-global remote mode (one unified `hermes serve`; desktop client attached via Settings → Gateway → Remote gateway), the Projects sidebar shows the serve's **launch-profile** projects regardless of the profile selected in the app. Sessions correctly follow the selected profile; projects do not.

## Impact

Remote clients can't see or manage per-profile projects. For users who organize work in projects/worktrees, the remote app is not a usable mirror of the backend — project management becomes host-only.

## Root cause

Per-profile isolation for projects currently happens *by process*: in local mode, the Electron main process routes each profile's calls to a pooled backend spawned with `--profile <name>` (each with its own `HERMES_HOME`). In app-global remote mode all profiles share one backend, so scoping must happen server-side per request — and for `projects.*` it doesn't:

- `tui_gateway/server.py` `projects.tree` handler calls `_get_db()` — always the launch profile's store.
- The scoping mechanism already exists: `_db_for_profile(profile)` (docstring: "App-global remote mode passes `profile` on session.* RPCs so history/list/create operate on that profile's state.db"). It was never applied to the `projects.*` namespace.
- The REST side shows the intended pattern: `GET /api/model/options` wraps its work in `_profile_scope(profile)`.

## Repro

1. Run `hermes serve -p default` (unified, multiple profiles). In profile B, create projects (`profiles/B/projects.db` has rows; the launch profile's `projects.db` has none).
2. Attach a remote desktop in app-global remote mode; select profile B.
3. Sidebar shows the launch profile's project tree.
4. Verified at the RPC level: `projects.tree` over `/api/ws` returns an identical tree for `params.profile` = B, `default`, or unset.

## Suggested fix

Apply the `_db_for_profile()` / `_profile_db` treatment to the whole `projects.*` namespace: `projects.tree`, `projects.project_sessions`, `projects.list`, `projects.for_cwd`, `projects.record_repos`, `projects.discover_repos`.

Note `projects.record_repos` additionally needs remote-mode thought: the repo scan runs client-side (Electron `scanRepos` on the client's disk) but records to the backend. For a thin remote client the valuable scan target is the *backend's* filesystem, and records should land in the scoped profile's `projects.db`.

## Version

0.19.0 (release 2026.7.20)

## Summary

When using a custom provider pointed at an Alibaba DashScope-compatible endpoint
(e.g. `https://token-plan.ap-southeast-1.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1`),
the `agent.reasoning_effort` config has **no effect** on the actual reasoning depth.

## Root Cause

The legacy flag path in `agent/transports/chat_completions.py` emits reasoning as:

```json
{ "extra_body": { "reasoning": { "enabled": true, "effort": "high" } } }
```

The DashScope backend **silently ignores** this nested object (accepts any value
including invalid ones like `"ultra"` with HTTP 200). It only honours the
**top-level flat parameter**:

```json
{ "reasoning_effort": "high" }
```

## Evidence

Tested directly against the endpoint with `qwen3.8-max-preview`:

| Parameter format | Server behaviour |
|---|---|
| `extra_body.reasoning.effort = "ultra"` | HTTP 200, silently ignored |
| Top-level `reasoning_effort = "ultra"` | HTTP 400: *"reasoning_effort must be one of: none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max"* |
| Top-level `reasoning_effort = "none"` | HTTP 400: *"enable_thinking parameter is restricted to True"* (thinking-only model) |
| Top-level `reasoning_effort = "low".."max"` | Accepted, reasoning_tokens vary |

## Valid values for DashScope

`minimal | low | medium | high | xhigh | max`

- `none` is rejected by thinking-only models (e.g. qwen3.8-max-preview)
- `ultra` does not exist on this backend

## Suggested Fix

Add a branch in `build_kwargs()` (legacy path) that detects custom providers on
`*.maas.aliyuncs.com` or `dashscope.*` base URLs and emits `reasoning_effort` as
a top-level `api_kwargs` parameter (same pattern as Kimi/TokenHub/LM Studio),
while skipping the `extra_body["reasoning"]` emission.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent (git install, Windows)
- Provider: `custom:qwen-token-plan`
- base_url: `https://token-plan.ap-southeast-1.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1`
- Model: `qwen3.8-max-preview`

items.title: [Bug]: search_files fails with absolute Windows paths when rg is a native Windows binary (MSYS path rewrite)

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
## Bug Description

On Windows, calling the `search_files` tool with an **absolute** Windows path (either `C:\...` or `C:/...`) always fails with `系统找不到指定的路径。 (os error 3)`. Relative paths work fine.

Reproduced across many sessions (July–August 2026). The tool rewrites the absolute path into MSYS form `/c/Users/...` and passes it to `rg`, but `rg` installed via WinGet is a **native Windows binary** and cannot resolve `/c/...` paths.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 (Dev Channel, ThinkPad X1C)
- Shell: Git Bash / MSYS (Hermes desktop app)
- rg: ripgrep 15.1.0 x86_64-pc-windows-msvc (installed via WinGet, `BurntSushi.ripgrep.MSVC`)
- Hermes: git-installed at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a Hermes session with cwd = `C:\Users\<user>\projects\<repo>`
2. Call `search_files` with `path = "C:/Users/<user>/projects/<repo>/stock_sim"` (absolute, forward slashes)
3. Observe failure

Actual output:

```
Search failed: rg: /c/Users/<user>/projects/<repo>/stock_sim: IO error for operation on /c/Users/<user>/projects/<repo>/stock_sim: 系统找不到指定的路径。 (os error 3)
```

Same failure with the backslash form `C:\Users\...` and when `path` points at a single file.

Relative paths work:

```
search_files(path="stock_sim/routes.py", pattern="def api_positions")   # OK
search_files(path=".", pattern="def api_positions", file_glob="routes.py")  # OK
```

## Root Cause

- `tools/environments/local.py` `_bash_safe_path()` (~line 111) rewrites `C:\...` / `C:/...` to MSYS form `/c/...` via `_windows_to_msys_path()`.
- `tools/file_operations.py` `_search_with_rg()` (~line 2236) and `_search_files_rg()` build bash command lines using `self._escape_shell_arg(path)`, which calls `_bash_safe_path` (local.py ~line 137).
- The resulting command runs `rg <path>` inside bash. When `rg` is a **native Windows binary**, it receives `/c/Users/...` and cannot resolve it → os error 3. MSYS tools (ls, sed, head) resolve `/c/...` fine, which is why the rewrite was introduced in the first place.
- Relative paths have no drive prefix, so `_windows_to_msys_path` leaves them untouched → search works. This asymmetry (absolute broken, relative fine) makes the bug confusing.

## Impact

- All `search_files` content searches and file listings fail on Windows when given absolute paths. Agents must work around it by passing relative paths or falling back to terminal `grep` / `read_file`.
- `read_file` / `write_file` / `patch` are **unaffected** (pure Python IO, no bash layer).

## Related

- #46876 (closed, `implemented_on_main`): different direction — file tools receiving MSYS *input* paths produced a `C:\c\...` ghost tree. That fix normalizes host-side `/c/...` paths in `tools/file_tools.py` but does **not** cover the search_files → rg call path (verified against current `main`; `_bash_safe_path` is still used there).

## Suggested Fix

When invoking native Windows binaries (`rg`) on Windows, do not apply the MSYS `/c/...` rewrite to path arguments — keep the forward-slash Windows form `C:/...`, or convert back via `cygpath -w` before exec. The MSYS rewrite should only apply to MSYS tools (or shell builtins) that actually understand `/c/...`.

items.title: GET /api/messaging/platforms blocks event loop for 6-12s, causes Desktop 'Messaging platforms failed to load' timeout

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/dashboard
labels.description: Web dashboard / control panel UI (dashboard/, landing)

items.body:
## Bug Description

`GET /api/messaging/platforms` blocks the FastAPI event loop for 6–12 seconds on every call, causing:
- Desktop app's "Messaging platforms failed to load" error (`Timed out connecting to Hermes backend after 15000ms`)
- Repeated `event loop stalled Ns (GIL pressure suspected)` warnings in `errors.log`, correlated in time with the request

## Root Cause

`get_messaging_platforms()` in `hermes_cli/web_server.py` (currently around line 9192) is declared `async def` but its body runs entirely synchronously on the event-loop thread — no `await`, no `run_in_threadpool`/`asyncio.to_thread`.

For every platform in `_messaging_platform_catalog()` (32 entries on a stock install: built-ins + plugin platforms like irc/ntfy/photon/simplex/raft/buzz/...), `_messaging_platform_payload()` is called synchronously, and each one calls `resolve_gateway_liveness()` (`gateway/status.py`), which does PID/process-table probing and file I/O per call. 32 sequential synchronous liveness probes on the event loop thread easily add up to multiple seconds and starve the loop for everyone else (hence the GIL-pressure-stall warnings and Desktop's 15s readiness timeout).

This is the same class of bug already fixed for `/api/status`'s profile/gateway topology scan (see the existing `_collect_profile_gateway_topology_cached` + `run_in_threadpool`/executor pattern added there) — `/api/messaging/platforms` was apparently missed by that fix.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Fresh/updated Hermes install with several messaging platform plugins present (default install already ships ~32 catalog entries).
2. Launch Hermes Desktop.
3. Open the Messaging / Channels page (or just let Desktop poll `/api/messaging/platforms` on boot).
4. Observe: request takes 6–12s; if it (or a concurrent poll) exceeds 15s, Desktop shows "Messaging platforms failed to load — Timed out connecting to Hermes backend after 15000ms".
5. `errors.log` shows `event loop stalled Ns (GIL pressure suspected)` around the same timestamps.

Direct repro (bypassing Desktop, hitting the backend directly with the dashboard session token):
```python
import time, urllib.request
req = urllib.request.Request(
    "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/messaging/platforms",
    headers={"X-Hermes-Session-Token": "<token>"},
)
t0 = time.perf_counter()
urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=20).read()
print(time.perf_counter() - t0)  # consistently ~6.6-8.5s on this machine
```

## Expected Behavior

`/api/messaging/platforms` should return quickly (sub-second) and must not block the event loop, matching the pattern already used for `/api/status`'s topology scan.

## Actual Behavior

- ~6.6–12.5s response time, reproduced consistently across multiple runs.
- Concurrent `event loop stalled Ns (GIL pressure suspected)` log entries during the call.
- Desktop app's readiness probe (15s timeout) intermittently fails with "Messaging platforms failed to load".

## Suggested Fix

Wrap the synchronous body of `get_messaging_platforms()` (and/or `_messaging_platform_payload()`'s liveness probing loop) in `starlette.concurrency.run_in_threadpool` / `asyncio.to_thread`, the same way the `/api/status` topology scan and `_load_configured_gateway_platforms()` were already moved off the event loop. Alternatively, cache `resolve_gateway_liveness()` per request (call it once, reuse across the 32 catalog entries) instead of once per platform, since it resolves to the same gateway state for all of them within a single request.

## Investigated and ruled out

This machine carries two small local (uncommitted) patches on top of `main` (`plugins/platforms/photon/adapter.py` + its test) that only change the upload filename for outbound iMessage voice notes (`send_voice`). They have no relation to `get_messaging_platforms`, `resolve_gateway_liveness`, or the event loop, and the same blocking behavior reproduces cleanly against unmodified `origin/main` at commit `c83ddd6a5`.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10
- Hermes Agent: v0.19.1, git install, commit `c83ddd6a5` (upstream `main`, current at time of report)
- Install method: git
- Python: 3.11.15
- Surface: Hermes Desktop (native app) talking to `hermes serve` backend

items.title: read_file misdetects valid UTF-8 (CJK) files as binary when 1000-byte sample cut lands mid-character

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
## Summary

`read_file` (and the internal full-file raw read used by `patch`) misclassify **valid UTF-8 files containing CJK text as binary**, returning `Binary file - cannot display as text...`, whenever the 1000-byte `head -c 1000` sample boundary lands in the middle of a multi-byte character.

## Root Cause

In `tools/file_operations.py`:

- `read_file` samples the file with `head -c 1000` — a **byte-based** truncation (line 1168).
- The sampled bytes are decoded by the terminal execution layer with `errors="replace"` (see comment at lines 887-895): a multi-byte sequence truncated at byte 1000 becomes a trailing **U+FFFD** replacement character.
- `_is_likely_binary` (line 875) then returns `True` when `"\ufffd" in content_sample[:1000]` (line 896), flagging a perfectly valid file as binary.

For CJK-heavy UTF-8 text (3-byte characters), the byte-1000 boundary has roughly a 2/3 chance of falling inside a multi-byte character, so this false positive is common.

The same check is reused by the full-file raw read at lines 1286-1292, so `patch` is affected too.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a UTF-8 `.md`/text file containing Chinese text longer than ~330 characters (so byte 1000 falls inside a CJK character).
2. Call `read_file` on it.
3. Actual: `Binary file - cannot display as text. Use appropriate tools to handle this file type.`

Real example: a 4,846-byte Chinese sports-news summary (pure UTF-8 — decodes with **zero** U+FFFD; `file` identifies it as `Unicode text, UTF-8 text`) was rejected. The 1000-byte boundary cut the character 决 (UTF-8 bytes `e5 86 b3`) after two bytes, leaving continuation byte `0x9b`, which decodes to a trailing U+FFFD.

## Expected Behavior

Valid UTF-8 text files should be readable regardless of CJK/multi-byte content.

## Suggested Fix

A truncated sequence produces exactly **one trailing** U+FFFD at the end of the sample; genuine corruption spreads U+FFFD throughout. Strip trailing replacement chars before the check:

```python
if "\ufffd" in content_sample[:1000].rstrip("\ufffd"):
    return True
```

Alternatively, fix the byte/character mismatch at the source: decode the sample with proper UTF-8 handling (e.g. cut at a character boundary, or decode bytes and only then apply the 1000-char window).

## Environment

- OS: Debian (Linux 6.12)
- hermes-agent installed at `/usr/local/lib/hermes-agent` (venv)
- Verified identical code on `main` branch (lines 875/896/1168/1286)

items.title: Tracking: core toolset performance batch — terminal & file-ops turn-efficiency (12 PRs)
items.body:
# Tracking: Core toolset performance batch — terminal & file-ops turn-efficiency improvements

Umbrella tracker for the 15-PR batch improving core tool performance (Aug 2, 2026). "Performance" here = fewer wasted tool turns, fewer model-confusing errors, smaller/clearer schemas — not just wall clock. All 15 PRs are open and ALL GREEN on CI (37–39 checks each). Hard A/B evaluation results (baseline vs all-fixes integration): see "Hard A/B evaluation" section below — weak model: −21% turns, −29% tool calls, errors→0, −23% wall clock; strong model: parity.

## Campaign infographic

![Core toolset performance batch — 16 PRs, methods, and headline numbers](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aa4c80b/bgTKR6RREinj2I_aHnw2H_7SGLLgXo.png)

## Methodology (shared by every PR)

- **Evidence mining:** production session DB (`state.db`, 1.53M messages, 33k sessions). Error taxonomy, retry-chain analysis, and duplicate-call detection over a recent 400k-message window plus a 250k-terminal-result window.
- **Live benchmark harness:** `hermes chat` battery (11 realistic tasks: multi-file refactor, patch dedup, big-file nav, venv state, bg server lifecycle, failure diagnosis, git flow, hint-targeted probes) traced through the **NeMo Relay** plugin (ATOF/ATIF export, nemo-relay 0.6.0). Scored per run: LLM calls, tool calls, tool errors, exact-duplicate calls, retry-after-error, result KB, wall time. Harness: `/tmp/hermes-toolperf/bench_tools.py`.
- **Baseline:** 8 tasks × 3 reps on sonnet-4.5: 19/24 ok, 195 LLM calls, 189 tool calls, 24 errors, 782s wall.
- **Design inputs:** tool-design surveys of 13 agent codebases (codex, claude-code, opencode, gemini-cli, crush, aider, swe-agent, goose, cline, roo-code, kimi-cli, qwen-code, openhands) + 15-item research synthesis (SWE-agent ACI, Anthropic tool-writing, TokenPilot, PALADIN, W&D, MAST, et al.).
- **Verification per PR:** unit tests → hermetic CI-parity runner (`scripts/run_tests.sh`) → live E2E through the real tool functions in an isolated `HERMES_HOME` → ATOF-traced bench where the battery covers the surface → full CI (37–39 checks).

All PRs below are **ALL GREEN** on CI unless noted.

---

## Terminal

### 1. #76992 — feat(terminal): output-pattern failure hints for common error classes
**Problem (mined):** ~14k failed calls in a 250k-call window fall into recognizable shapes — gh `Unknown JSON field` 9,175 / merge conflict 1,172 / command-not-found 1,010 (bare `python` 837) / ModuleNotFoundError 739 / `already exists` 633 / gh rate limit 133 — with 3,697 same-tool retry-after-error turns chained behind them.
**Fix:** bounded 4KB output scan → one actionable `hint` field (10 classes + exit-code tier 124/126/137); suppressed when `exit_code_meaning` already explains (grep=1 etc).
**Benchmark report:** unit 18/18; combined terminal suites 42 passed; live E2E: python→python3 hint, venv import hint, which/install hint, grep-no-match correctly hint-free. A/B battery (3 hint-targeted tasks × 4 reps): 12/12 ok both arms, identical turn counts on sonnet-4.5 (strong models already recover in 1 turn — hints target the production long tail and weaker models); no regression, wall 159s (on) vs 184s (off).

### 2. #77004 — feat(terminal): echo cwd in result when a command changes the working directory
**Problem (mined):** 60.2% of 104,507 terminal calls carry a defensive `cd X && ` prefix (~925k tokens of prefix in one window); 2,462 failed calls led with `cd`; dir changes followed by `pwd`/`ls` verification turns.
**Fix:** result gains `"cwd"` whenever the session cwd changed (realpath compare, symlink-safe); stable commands byte-identical; per-command `workdir` stays transient. Schema note: trust it, drop the prefixes. (crush `<cwd>` pattern.)
**Benchmark report:** hermetic 25/25; live E2E: cd echoes, `ls` after cd silent + correct dir, chained `cd a && cd b` reports final dir, failed cd silent. Battery (term_state/git_flow/diag_fail × 2): 6/6 ok, 26 LLM calls vs 28 baseline for same tasks.

### 3. #77017 — fix(terminal): blocked-command errors carry a concrete recovery recipe
**Problem (mined):** parser-limit/malformed-payload hardline blocks (198×) fire on oversized inline payloads, not forbidden ops — but read as a permanent ban; `&`/nohup/setsid blocks (200×) described the feature abstractly. Both answered with blind rephrase-retries.
**Fix:** parser-limit block appends RECOVERY recipe (write_file → `bash script.sh`, don't retry inline); backgrounding blocks show the literal corrected call shape. Genuine hardline blocks (destructive ops) unchanged. No policy loosened.
**Benchmark report:** hermetic 105/105 (new + approval + terminal suites); live E2E: 5KB separator-free payload → block WITH recipe; `http.server &` → exact-call-shape guidance. Meta-validation: the hardline detector blocked this PR's own first commit message for naming a forbidden command — guard intact.

### 4. #77041 — feat(terminal): recoverable truncation — spill full output + report pre-truncation size
**Problem (mined):** 1,394 truncation markers in a 250k-call window; the omitted middle was permanent loss — only recovery was re-running the command.
**Fix:** `_BoundedOutputCollector` tees overflow to `~/.hermes/cache/terminal-output/out-*.log` (lazy creation + backlog backfill, 5MB cap, 7-day cleanup, redacted with the same pass as visible output, OSError-proof); result carries `output_total_chars`, `full_output_path`, and a note steering to search_files/read_file. Spill only arms on the foreground bounded-capture path; non-truncated results byte-identical. (opencode/goose/qwen-code spill + codex pre-truncation size.)
**Benchmark report:** hermetic 94/94 (spill + terminal + base/docker/ssh env suites); live E2E: 326,507-char output at the real 50KB cap → spill holds every byte incl. cut middle rows; `search_files` on the spill finds a cut line; secret planted in the overflow region absent from spill after redaction.

### 5. #77023 — refactor(schema): trim terminal and execute_code schema prose ~40%
**Problem (measured):** schemas ship on every API call; 88 registered tools ≈ 33k tokens. Terminal largest core offender at 5,641 chars (~1,410 tok) — notify/background contract stated 3×, padded with war stories.
**Fix:** terminal desc 2,324→1,233 chars; background/notify_on_complete/watch_patterns params 692/508/1,114 → ~330/250/490; execute_code desc tightened. Every hard rule kept, stated once.
**Benchmark report:** measured via live registry import: terminal 5,641→3,386 chars, execute_code 2,842→2,522 — **~700 tokens saved per request** carrying these toolsets. Hermetic 66/66; battery (bg_server/term_state/edit_dedup × 2): 6/6 ok — background/notify behavior intact (bg_server still uses background=true + readiness check correctly).

## File ops

### 6. #76996 — feat(file): raise read_file default limit from 500 to 2000 lines
**Problem (mined):** 74.3% of 28.5k reads truncated — 22,443 by the 500-line default vs **13** by the char budget. 12,229 redundant re-reads; after truncation the #1 next move was fleeing to terminal `cat`/`sed` (4,608×) — pagination distrust. Median truncated file = 2,422 total lines (p90 15k).
**Fix:** default 500→2000 (already the schema max) across `DEFAULT_READ_LIMIT`, both `read_file()` signatures, tool schema, execute_code sandbox stubs. The ~100K char budget stays as the hard ceiling (worst case unchanged: 500 × 2000-char line cap = same 100K).
**Benchmark report:** 44% of today's truncated first-reads become complete in one call. Targeted suites 149 passed; live E2E: 1,800-line file complete in one read (was 4 pages), 5,000-line file truncates at 2000 with `offset=2001` hint, 450KB wide file → char budget fires (`truncated_by: bytes`) — ceiling intact. Battery: 4/4 ok, no regression.

### 7. #76998 — feat(patch): detect already-applied edits and return success no-op
**Problem (mined):** #1 patch failure class = replay of an already-landed edit: `old_string and new_string are identical` (299×) + share of 299 hunk-not-found where new text already present; 622 success_false results; each spawned re-read/re-patch loops.
**Fix:** conservative `is_already_applied()` (new_string ≥8 chars, EXACT presence, old gone unless identical) → `success + no_change: true` + "do not re-send" note in replace mode; V4A validation AND apply phases skip already-applied hunks (multi-hunk patches no longer fail wholesale). Genuine misses and half-applied renames still error.
**Benchmark report:** hermetic 43/43 + targeted 134 passed; live E2E: identical+present → no-op note; landed-rename replay → no-op; genuine miss → error; V4A mixed patch → live hunk applied, landed hunk skipped, file correct. Battery (edit_dedup/refactor × 2): 4/4 ok — refactor task dropped from 33–41 LLM calls (baseline) to 5.

### 8. #77001 — feat(patch): list match locations in ambiguous old_string errors
**Problem (mined):** `Found N matches` (190+×) reported only the count → standard recovery was read_file → locate → retry (2 extra turns for info the tool had in hand).
**Fix:** error appends up to 5 `L<line>: <snippet>` rows (80-char cap, overflow noted); shared by replace + V4A modes via `fuzzy_find_and_replace`.
**Benchmark report:** targeted 80 passed; live E2E on a 3-duplicate file: error carries `L2/L6/L10` rows. Battery (edit_dedup × 3): 3/3 ok, turn counts unchanged.

### 9. #77024 — feat(patch): whitespace-visualized diagnosis on residual no-match errors
**Problem:** the failure class that survives all 9 fuzzy strategies is tabs-vs-spaces/indent drift + a content diff — the did-you-mean hint showed the right lines but not WHY the match failed, so models guessed again.
**Fix:** when the best candidate matches after stripping but differs raw, append `file has: →def start(self):` vs `you sent: ····def start(self):` (→=tab, ·=space) + "use the exact whitespace shown". (crush `diagnoseMismatch` port.) Content-shaped misses unchanged.
**Benchmark report:** hermetic 127/127; live E2E on tab-indented file with space-indented old_string: error carries numbered did-you-mean block AND the glyph diagnosis.

### 10. #77055 — feat(file): verify write_file content on disk, report `verified: true`
**Problem (mined):** write_file confirmed only size (`wc -c`); models verify-read files right after writing (154×/window); corrupted writes could pass silently. patch_replace already verified — write_file didn't.
**Fix:** on-disk sha256 vs intended-content hash (one shell call). Match → `verified: true` + schema contract "do NOT re-read to check the write landed"; mismatch → hard error mirroring patch's check; no hasher → flag omitted, write unaffected. Hashes shim-adjusted content so CRLF/BOM round-trips verify.
**Benchmark report:** hermetic 104/104; live E2E: small py file verified + lint ok; 65KB unicode file verified; patch through the same write path unaffected; forced hash-mismatch → hard error; hasher failure never breaks the write.

## Search

### 11. #77011 — feat(search): zero-match probes and multi-path recovery
**Problem (mined + bench-discovered):** 13.9% of 19.6k content searches returned bare 0 matches (dead turn); 122 `Path not found` failures from multi-path strings; the benchmark battery caught a live miss — a match inside `.hidden/` returned bare 0 and the model missed the file in 2/3 baseline runs.
**Fix:** three bounded probes on clean 0-match results — case-insensitive count, hidden/gitignored count (`rg --hidden --no-ignore`), literal-vs-regex — attach one steering `warning`; true zeros stay clean. Multi-path strings split/searched/merged with skipped-paths note.
**Benchmark report:** hermetic 57/57 + 103 targeted; live E2E: case hint, hidden-file hint, multi-path merge with skip note, normal searches unchanged. Battery search_misc: 0/3 → **3/3 ok** after the hidden probe (validated with corrected scorer).

### 13. #77095 — feat(skills): dedup repeat skill_view calls with an unchanged-content stub
**Problem (mined):** skill_view re-sent full content on every call — ~286k tokens of verbatim repeat views in one 400k-msg window (one session loaded the same skill 9×).
**Fix:** per-task cache keyed on (resolved name, file_path) with mtime+size fingerprint; repeat view of an UNCHANGED file returns a short stub pointing at the earlier in-context result. Skills-load-fully rule preserved: on-disk change invalidates, context compression clears the cache (wired beside reset_file_dedup), setup-needed views never dedup, task-isolated.
**Benchmark report:** hermetic 128/128; live E2E on the real skills dir: first view of hermes-agent-dev = 99,739 chars, repeat = 374-char stub (~24.8k tokens saved per repeat); linked-file views dedup independently.

### 14. #77102 — feat(search): auto-enable multiline mode for newline patterns
**Problem (mined):** `\n` in a content pattern hard-errored in rg's line-oriented mode (17× in the window) — cross-line intent required manual rework.
**Fix:** the rg engine detects the pattern shape (odd-backslash `\n` escape or raw newline; escaped `\\n` literals excluded) and enables `-U/--multiline` up front, noting the switch in the result. Plain patterns untouched; grep fallback keeps the explanatory warning.
**Benchmark report:** hermetic 98/98; live E2E: previously-erroring `def start\(self\):\n        boot\(\)` → 2 matches + mode note; plain search unchanged.

### 15. #77106 — feat(execute_code): recovery hints for known sandbox failure classes
**Problem (mined):** top sandbox failures are contract confusions — hermes_tools import misuse (23×, incl. importing built-in helpers), stdlib-only ModuleNotFoundError (matplotlib 6×), dict-vs-string result handling.
**Fix:** failed scripts carry one actionable session-aware `hint` (lists the tools actually importable this session; redirects built-in helpers; points third-party imports at terminal()+venv; explains dict results). Bounded 4KB scan, first match wins, never raises; success paths untouched.
**Benchmark report:** hermetic 67/67; live sandbox E2E (real UDS child): bad import → hint naming it; missing module → stdlib hint; clean script → no hint field.

## Process

### 12. #77013 — fix(process): wait timeout result reads as status, not failure
**Problem (mined):** `process` is the #1 exact-duplicate tool call (511×/window; `wait` = 57% of process actions, 1,536 calls). Timeout results read as errors → identical re-waits.
**Fix:** timeout branch gains `process_running: true` + "Wait window of Ns elapsed — still running. This is not an error. Uptime: Ms." + notify-aware next step (notified-on-exit vs pointer to notify_on_complete). Clamp note composes instead of replacing. Exited/interrupted unchanged.
**Benchmark report:** hermetic 59/59; live E2E (real bg sleep → wait → kill): correct status fields + full note with uptime.

---

## Hard A/B evaluation (baseline = origin/main, fixes = all-15-PR integration branch)

**Setup:** 9 error-inducing tasks derived from the mined production waste classes × 2 models × 2 arms × 3 reps (108 runs + 6 re-runs after purging startup-crashed records). Arms differ ONLY by PYTHONPATH; integration branch passed 141/141 combined tests. Metrics from NeMo Relay ATOF traces. Harness: `/tmp/hermes-abeval/ab_eval.py` (reproducible via `run_all.sh`).

### Aggregate

| model | arm | ok% | llm turns | tool calls | tool errs | retries | result KB | wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| qwen3-coder-30b (weak) | baseline | 74% | 3.8 | 2.8 | 0.1 | 0.1 | 12 | 22s |
| qwen3-coder-30b (weak) | **fixes** | 67% | **3.0 (−21%)** | **2.0 (−29%)** | **0.0** | **0.0** | **8 (−33%)** | **17s (−23%)** |

| sonnet-4.5 (strong) | fixes | 85% | 2.9 | 2.2 | 0.0 | 0.0 | 19 | 15s |

### Per-task highlights (weak model, where the waste manifests)

| task (targets PR) | baseline | fixes |
|---|---|---|
| err_python_env (#76992 hints) | 6.7 turns, 0.7 errs, 23s | **3.3 turns, 0 errs, 14s** |
| err_case_search (#77011 probe) | 4.0 turns | **3.0 turns** |
| err_big_file_read (#76996 limit) | 5.0 turns, 88KB, 75s | **3.7 turns, 51KB, 39s** |

### Honest readout

- **Weak model: clear, consistent efficiency win** across every metric — this is the population the hint/limit/probe PRs target.
- **Strong model: parity.** Sonnet already one-turns most induced errors; deltas are within n=3 noise (89 vs 85% ok = 1 run), and the fixes add no slowdown.
- **Sub-100% fixes cells audited run-by-run:** 6 first-pass sonnet/fixes records were eval-infra startup crashes (purged + re-run clean); one grading marker had wrong expected arithmetic (fixed); the rest are single-run strict-answer misses on n=3.

- **Dropped:** opencode's disproportionate-match guard for patch — empirical testing (incl. a sabotage run with the guard disabled) proved Hermes' block_anchor (0.5/0.7 similarity thresholds) and context_aware (all-lines ≥0.80) strategies cannot produce the overmatch it defends against. Dead code refused.
- **Backlog: fully resolved.** Shipped: skill_view dedup (#77095), search auto-multiline (#77102), execute_code sandbox hints (#77106). Declined with data: auto-`ls` on cwd change (0.2% follow-up rate in production — mined 1,255 cd commands); read_file error-vs-truncate economics (our char budget fires on 0.04% of reads — 15/40,000 — nothing to tune); gh JSON-field preflight (#76992's hint already 1-turns it; a preflight special-cases one CLI inside the terminal tool — wrong footprint); per-model schema overrides (speculative until the A/B eval surfaces a measured per-model divergence).
