items.body:
When a session uses gpt-5.6-luna via openai-codex (which had streaming failures) alongside delegate_task subagents, the relay runtime's scope stack gets corrupted. Turn finalization fails silently with:

RuntimeError: invalid argument: scope handle is not at the top of the stack File "relay_runtime.py", line 644, in end_turn File "nemo_relay/scope.py", line 144, in pop _native_pop_scope(handle, output=output, metadata=metadata, timestamp=timestamp)

Once corrupted, every subsequent turn-finalization fails — the assistant's response is generated but never delivered to the user. From the user's perspective, the session freezes indefinitely.

Steps to reproduce
Start a session with gpt-5.6-luna via openai-codex (model switch mid-session from deepseek-v4-flash/opencode-go)
Dispatch parallel delegations via delegate_task
Wait for the Codex provider to hit a streaming failure (Codex Responses stream did not emit a terminal response)
Observe: session stops responding on subsequent turns, even after model retries succeed
Expected behavior
Scope-stack errors should be caught and recovered. Turn finalization should never silently drop the response. At minimum, the user should see an error message rather than an indefinite hang.

Actual behavior
Assistant appears to freeze — no response delivered for 25+ minutes
Error only visible in ~/.hermes/logs/errors.log
Two scope-stack crashes recorded at 09:59:18 and 10:25:15 in the same session
User forced to abandon session and start a new one
Environment
Hermes: 0.19.1 [21040c4a] (2026-08-03) OS: Windows 10 AMD64 Python: 3.11.15 Profile: default (config version 33) Model: default=deepseek-v4-flash, crashed session used gpt-5.6-luna Provider: default=opencode-go, crashed session used openai-codex

Relevant log excerpts
2026-08-04 09:51:35 WARNING Codex streaming attempt superseded by a newer stream 2026-08-04 09:51:35 WARNING API call failed: Codex Responses stream did not emit a terminal response (attempt 1/3) 2026-08-04 09:51:35 WARNING Retrying API call in 2.36s (attempt 1/3)

2026-08-04 09:59:18 WARNING Hermes Relay turn finalization failed RuntimeError: invalid argument: scope handle is not at the top of the stack File "nemo_relay/scope.py", line 144, in pop

2026-08-04 10:25:15 WARNING Hermes Relay turn finalization failed RuntimeError: invalid argument: scope handle is not at the top of the stack File "nemo_relay/scope.py", line 144, in pop

Workaround
Avoid openai-codex / gpt-5.6-luna in sessions that use delegate_task. Stick to opencode-go / deepseek-v4-flash. Restarting the session (not just /reset) clears the corrupted scope stack.

items.title: [Bug] clarify tool free-text response intermittently fails to bind to pending clarify call, hanging the turn indefinitely

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
### Environment
```
version:  0.19.1 [1f8acb34] (2026-08-03)
os:       Linux 6.17.4-2-pve x86_64
python:   3.11.15
profile:  default
model:    claude-sonnet-5
provider: anthropic
platforms: discord, homeassistant
gateway:  systemd-managed (hermes-gateway.service)
```

### Description
When a `clarify()` tool call is pending (the agent asked the user to pick an option or type a custom answer) and the user responds with **free text** (not a button click), the gateway is supposed to intercept that text and route it back to the waiting `clarify()` call — logged as `"Gateway intercepted clarify text response"`. This worked correctly 3 times in one session tonight, but failed silently a 4th time: the user's text arrived as a normal message with no interception log line, and the agent's turn stayed blocked on the open `clarify()` call indefinitely (no timeout, no error, no response) until the gateway was restarted.

### Steps to reproduce
Not reliably reproducible yet — intermittent. Occurred once in ~4 attempts within the same session.
1. Trigger a `clarify()` tool call with both button options and a free-text fallback.
2. Respond with free text (not a button click) in Discord.
3. Compare gateway.log for the presence/absence of `"Gateway intercepted clarify text response"` following the message.

### Actual behavior (successful cases, for comparison)
```
2026-08-03 21:26:33,280 INFO gateway.run: Gateway intercepted clarify text response (session=agent:main:discord:dm:<chat_id>, id=d706896467)
2026-08-03 21:26:33,280 INFO [<session_id>] agent.tool_executor: tool clarify completed (64.94s, 465 chars)
```

### Actual behavior (failed case)
```
2026-08-03 22:53:38,335 INFO hermes_plugins.discord_platform.adapter: [Discord] Flushing text batch agent:main:discord:dm:<chat_id> (146 chars)
2026-08-03 22:53:38,972 INFO gateway.run: inbound message: platform=discord user=tofuug chat=<chat_id> msg='lets continue those paused jobs. they were pinging me every 15 minutes because o' reply_to_id=None reply_to_text=''
```
No `"Gateway intercepted clarify text response"` line follows. No `tool clarify completed` line follows. The agent had issued `clarify()` moments earlier (mid-turn, in-flight at the time). The turn never completed; no response was ever sent for this message. The gateway had to be restarted to recover.

### Expected behavior
- Free-text clarify responses should reliably bind to the pending clarify call every time, not intermittently.
- If binding fails or times out, the agent should fail the turn visibly (error message to the user) rather than hang silently forever with no user-facing indication anything is wrong.

### Suspected root cause
Possible race between the Discord text-batcher flush (`[Discord] Flushing text batch ...`, which coalesces rapid messages before delivery) and the clarify-interception check — if the pending-clarify lookup happens before the batched message is fully routed, or if there's a session-key mismatch under concurrent load, the text could fall through to normal message handling instead of being intercepted.

### Workaround
`systemctl restart hermes-gateway` unblocks the stuck turn. No workaround exists to prevent the race from occurring in the first place; a fresh clarify() call after restart would need to be re-issued by the agent.

### Related
Likely related root-cause category to the turn-finalization crash reported separately (scope handle corruption on interrupt) — both are concurrency/interrupt edge cases in turn lifecycle management that leave sessions silently hung with no user-facing signal.

items.title: sanitize_api_messages does not catch tool messages with missing/empty tool_call_id

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

Follow-up finding from #78063 (which fixes #77921's stale `tool_calls: []` merge gap). While auditing `repair_message_sequence` / `sanitize_api_messages` for other unaudited corruption paths, found that the pre-API chokepoint sanitizer does not filter tool messages carrying a missing or empty `tool_call_id`.

## Root Cause

In `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py`, `sanitize_api_messages()` builds its orphan-detection set like this:

```python
result_call_ids: set = set()
for msg in messages:
    if msg.get("role") == "tool":
        cid = (msg.get("tool_call_id") or "").strip()
        if cid:
            result_call_ids.add(cid)
```

A tool message with a missing/empty `tool_call_id` produces `cid = ""`, which is falsy and is **never added** to `result_call_ids`. The subsequent orphan-removal step only drops ids present in `orphaned_results = result_call_ids - surviving_call_ids` — since the empty-id message was never added to `result_call_ids`, it can never land in `orphaned_results` either. The message passes through `sanitize_api_messages` completely untouched and can reach the provider with a missing/empty `tool_call_id`, which strict OpenAI-compatible providers (DeepSeek, Kimi) reject as a schema violation.

`repair_message_sequence`'s Pass 1 (same file) *does* correctly drop this case:

```python
elif role == "tool":
    tc_id = msg.get("tool_call_id")
    if tc_id and tc_id in known_tool_ids:
        filtered.append(msg)
        known_tool_ids.discard(tc_id)
    else:
        repairs += 1   # dropped — tc_id falsy or unknown
```

So in the main conversation loop, where `repair_message_sequence_with_cursor` runs before `sanitize_api_messages` is called on the derived `api_messages` copy, this is currently masked. The gap is real defense-in-depth exposure for any call site that invokes `sanitize_api_messages` (or `AIAgent._sanitize_api_messages`) on a message list that did **not** first pass through `repair_message_sequence` — e.g. the summary path in `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py:2166`, or any future caller. `sanitize_api_messages`'s own docstring says it "Runs unconditionally... so orphans from session loading or manual message manipulation are always caught" — this case isn't.

## Suggested Fix

In `sanitize_api_messages`, treat a tool message with an empty/missing `tool_call_id` as unconditionally orphaned (drop it), independent of the `result_call_ids` / `surviving_call_ids` set-difference logic — mirroring the `if tc_id and tc_id in known_tool_ids` guard `repair_message_sequence` Pass 1 already uses.

## Scope note

Deliberately not included in #78063 — that PR is scoped to the `repair_message_sequence` consecutive-assistant-merge stale-field gap (`tool_calls` and, per its follow-up commit, `api_content`). This is a separate defense-in-depth gap in a different function (`sanitize_api_messages`) and different failure trigger (missing id vs. stale merge artifact).

items.title: [Bug] Custom provider: model.provider gets set to display name (e.g. "custom:9router") instead of runtime name ("custom:Custom"), causing "Unknown provider" error

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Bug Description
When selecting a custom provider from the `hermes model` menu (or via `hermes setup`), the `model.provider` config value is incorrectly set to the **display name** from `custom_providers[i].name` (e.g., `"9router"`, `"custom"`, `"agent"`) instead of the actual runtime provider name defined in `providers.custom.name` (which is `"Custom"`).

This causes an `Unknown provider 'custom:9router'` error on startup/chat because the runtime only knows the provider registered as `custom:Custom`.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run `hermes model` and select "Custom endpoint (enter URL manually)" (option 36/37)
2. Enter a name like `9router`, base_url `http://localhost:20128/v1`, model `agent`
3. Repeat step 1-2 two more times with different names (`custom`, `agent`) — this creates duplicate entries in `custom_providers`
4. Select one of the custom entries from the menu (e.g., `9router`)
5. Check `config.yaml` → `model.provider` shows `custom:9router` ❌
6. Run `hermes chat` or `hermes doctor` → Error: `Unknown provider 'custom:9router'`

## Expected Behavior
`model.provider` should always be set to `custom:Custom` (matching `providers.custom.name`), regardless of which `custom_providers` entry was selected in the menu. The display name is only for UI; the runtime provider name is fixed as `Custom`.

## Actual Behavior
`model.provider` gets set to `custom:<display_name>` (e.g., `custom:9router`, `custom:custom`, `custom:agent`), which doesn't exist in the provider registry.

## Environment
- OS: Windows 10
- Hermes Version: 0.19.1 (also present in 0.20.0)
- Shell: MSYS/Git-Bash
- Config: Custom provider pointing to local OpenAI-compatible endpoint (9router on localhost:20128)

## Config Example (Broken State)
```yaml
model:
  provider: custom:9router    # ❌ Wrong - should be custom:Custom
  default: agent
  base_url: http://localhost:20128/v1

providers:
  custom:
    name: Custom              # Runtime name is "Custom"
    base_url: http://localhost:20128/v1
    model: agent

custom_providers:
  - name: 9router             # Display name only
    base_url: http://localhost:20128/v1
    ...
  - name: custom              # Duplicate from re-adding
    ...
  - name: agent               # Duplicate from re-adding
    ...
```

## Workaround
Manually fix `config.yaml`:
```bash
sed -i 's/provider: custom:.*/provider: custom:Custom/' ~/AppData/Local/hermes/config.yaml
```

## Additional Context
- The `custom_providers` list accumulates duplicates every time user "removes and re-adds" the API key/endpoint via the menu
- There's no "Update existing" logic — only "Add new"
- The UI shows the display name (e.g., "9router") but the runtime expects `providers.custom.name` ("Custom")

items.title: Windows: venv-blocker preflight still aborts desktop Update for .hermes-runtime gateways — cmdline truncated at 120 chars defeats the pausable-gateway exemption added by #75881

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
## Summary

#75881 ("let Windows desktop updates pause gateway processes instead of aborting") fixed the desktop Update flow for venv-side gateways, but on my machine the desktop Update button **still aborts with `venv-blocked` every time**, pointing at the gateway process. Root cause: the exemption check added by #75881 runs against a **cmdline truncated to 120 characters**, and the gateway launched from the desktop runtime's `.hermes-runtime\python\generation-...\cpython-...` path has a cmdline of **186 characters** — so the trailing `gateway run` tokens are cut off and the process is no longer recognized as a pausable gateway. The abort happens before the CLI updater's own `_pause_windows_gateways_for_update()` ever runs.

Verified on a HEAD that already contains #75881 (`d79a6f0e3`, v0.19.1, merge `d358edd9169e` present).

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.19.1 (2026-07-30), git install, HEAD `d79a6f0e3` — `git merge-base --is-ancestor d358edd9169e HEAD` → YES (fix is in)
- Windows 10
- Gateway installed as Scheduled Task (`Hermes_Gateway`), running as:

```
venv\Scripts\pythonw.exe -m hermes_cli.main gateway run
  └─ .hermes-runtime\python\generation-1785179197-21284-2ba3099e\cpython-3.11-windows-x86_64-none\python.exe -m hermes_cli.main gateway run   (PID reported as blocker)
```

## Root cause

`hermes_cli/update_cmd.py:2914` — `_detect_venv_python_processes()` truncates every reported cmdline:

```python
matches.append((int(pid), str(name), cmdline_raw[:120]))
```

`hermes_cli/_scan_venv_blockers.py:150` then applies the pausable-gateway exemption (added by #75881) to that **already-truncated** string:

```python
for pid, name, cmdline in matches
if not _is_pausable_gateway(cmdline)
```

`_is_pausable_gateway` → `gateway.status.looks_like_gateway_command_line` → `_gateway_command_subcommand`, which needs to see the `gateway` / `run` tokens to classify the process.

For a desktop-runtime gateway the executable path alone is longer than 120 chars:

```
"C:\Users\...\hermes-agent\.hermes-runtime\python\generation-1785179197-21284-2ba3099e\cpython-3.11-windows-x86_64-none\python.exe" -m hermes_cli.main gateway run
```

Measured on this machine:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| full cmdline length | 186 chars |
| `looks_like_gateway_command_line(full)` | **True** |
| `looks_like_gateway_command_line(full[:120])` | **False** |

So the gateway is reported as a non-pausable blocker, the Electron preflight (`venv-blocker-scan.ts` → `main.ts` `scanVenvBlockers` path) aborts with `venv-blocked`, and the CLI updater that knows how to pause/resume the gateway is never spawned. Symptom dialog: "Update aborted: another Hermes process is using this installation … must be stopped before updating: PID … python.exe …".

The CLI path (`hermes update`) is unaffected because it pauses gateways via `_pause_windows_gateways_for_update()` / `find_gateway_pids()` rather than this scan, and `_leftover_pausable_gateway_pids()` (update_cmd.py:3046-3054) already re-reads the **full argv** with psutil before classifying — the same pattern the preflight scan is missing.

## Suggested fix

Two candidate spots (either resolves it):

1. **`hermes_cli/_scan_venv_blockers.py`** — re-read the full argv with psutil before the exemption check, mirroring `_leftover_pausable_gateway_pids()` in `update_cmd.py` (3046-3054). Smallest change; keeps the 120-char cap for display only.
2. **`hermes_cli/update_cmd.py:2914`** — stop truncating what the matcher sees: keep the full cmdline in the match tuple and truncate only when formatting the holder message.

## Workaround (until fixed)

The CLI updater handles this correctly, so on Windows:

1. Close the Hermes Desktop app (its `serve` backend also holds venv `.pyd` files and the CLI refuses while it is running).
2. Run `hermes update --yes` in a terminal. It prints `→ Stopping Windows gateway process(es) before updating Hermes...`, pauses the gateway, updates, and auto-resumes it (`✓ Starting Windows gateway after update`).
3. Reopen the Desktop app.

Or, staying in the Desktop UI: `hermes gateway stop` before clicking Update, then `hermes gateway start` afterwards.

## Related

- #75881 — merged fix that introduced the exemption but is defeated by the truncation
- #74386, #74326, #74783 — the original three-layer gateway/update coordination issues, all auto-closed as COMPLETED by #75881 but this desktop-path failure persists on gateway-enabled installs

items.title: Desktop app silently exits when SingletonLock held by zombie/defunct Electron process (Linux/X11)
items.body:
## Bug: Desktop app silently exits when SingletonLock is held by a zombie Electron process (Linux/X11)

### Summary

When the Hermes Desktop Electron process becomes a zombie/defunct (e.g. after a crash, OOM kill, or `kill -9`), the `SingletonLock` in `~/.config/Hermes/` still points to the dead PID. The next launch via `hermes desktop` (or the `.desktop` shortcut) **silently exits with code 0** — no error message, no window, no log entry indicating the problem. The user sees nothing happen.

### Environment

- **OS:** Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 7.0.0-28-generic)
- **Session:** GNOME on X11
- **Hermes:** v0.19.1 (upstream 91937a6d, local b1858f33)
- **Electron:** 40.10.2
- **Install method:** git (`~/.hermes/hermes-agent/`)
- **GPU:** AMD Radeon RX 6600 (radeonsi, navi23)

### Reproduction

1. Launch `hermes desktop` — it works, window appears.
2. Kill the Electron process abruptly: `kill -9 <hermes-electron-pid>`
3. The `SingletonLock` symlink remains in `~/.config/Hermes/SingletonLock -> <hostname>-<dead-pid>`.
4. Launch `hermes desktop` again (or click the `.desktop` shortcut).
5. **Nothing happens.** The process exits immediately with code 0. No window, no error.

### Root cause

In `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts` (line ~11628):

```typescript
const _gotSingleInstanceLock = app.requestSingleInstanceLock()

if (!_gotSingleInstanceLock) {
  app.quit()
}
```

Electron's `requestSingleInstanceLock()` on Linux creates a `SingletonLock` symlink in the user data dir (`~/.config/Hermes/`). When the lock exists but points to a dead PID, Electron still treats it as a valid lock on some X11/Linux setups — `requestSingleInstanceLock()` returns `false`, and the app calls `app.quit()` immediately with no user feedback.

The `second-instance` handler (line ~11633) never fires because there IS no running first instance — the lock is stale.

### Evidence from logs

`~/.hermes/logs/desktop.log` shows the boot sequence completing successfully, then the process exits:

```
[hermes] [boot] Resolving Hermes backend
[hermes] [boot] Hermes runtime is ready
[hermes] [boot] Starting Hermes backend via Hermes at /home/jr0237/.hermes/hermes-agent
[hermes] HERMES_BACKEND_READY port=43543
[hermes] [boot] Hermes backend is ready. Finalizing desktop startup
```

No error, no crash — just silent exit. The backend starts fine but the Electron process quits because `requestSingleInstanceLock()` returned `false`.

The `SingletonLock` state observed:

```
$ ls -la ~/.config/Hermes/SingletonLock
lrwxrwxrwx 1 jr0237 jr0237 20 ago  3 20:44 ~/.config/Hermes/SingletonLock -> jr0237-MS-7A38-86682
# PID 86682 was alive but the window was invisible/broken (zombie X11 window)
```

### Suggested fix

Electron's `requestSingleInstanceLock()` is known to leave stale locks on Linux when the process dies abnormally. Options:

1. **Before calling `app.quit()` on lock failure**, check if the PID in the `SingletonLock` symlink target is actually alive. If the PID is dead, remove the stale lock files (`SingletonLock`, `SingletonCookie`, `SingletonSocket`) and retry `requestSingleInstanceLock()`. This is the approach used by VS Code and other Electron apps.

2. **At startup**, proactively validate any existing `SingletonLock` — if it points to a dead PID, clean it up before attempting to acquire the lock.

3. **Log a message** when `requestSingleInstanceLock()` returns `false` so the failure is visible in `desktop.log` (currently it is completely silent).

### Workaround

```bash
# Check for stale lock
ls -la ~/.config/Hermes/SingletonLock
# If the PID in the symlink target is dead, remove the lock files:
rm -f ~/.config/Hermes/SingletonLock ~/.config/Hermes/SingletonCookie ~/.config/Hermes/SingletonSocket
# Then launch normally
hermes desktop --skip-build
```

### Additional context

- The `.desktop` file at `~/.local/share/applications/hermes-desktop.desktop` is valid and correctly configured.
- The `desktop-file-validate` only shows a minor hint about Categories.
- The Electron binary and all libs are present in `apps/desktop/release/linux-unpacked/`.
- This is a Linux/X11-specific issue; macOS handles stale locks differently via macOS process singleton mechanisms.

items.title: Conversational task-closure has no structural effect on session state — compounding compression drift on abandoned sessions (session_reset.mode: none default)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug: conversational "this task is done" has no effect on session state — only `/reset`/`/new` do, so `session_reset.mode: none` (the current default) lets abandoned-but-acknowledged-closed sessions drift indefinitely

### Summary

`SessionResetPolicy.mode` defaults to `"none"` as of the July 2026 change (`gateway/config.py`, `SessionResetPolicy` docstring), so sessions never auto-reset unless the user opts in. That's a reasonable default for users who want persistent context. The problem is the *only* way to end a session is a structural trigger (`/reset`, `/new`, or an opted-in `session_reset` policy) — there's no path from "the user said in plain language that the task is done" to any actual state change. The agent will happily keep replying "Task acknowledged and marked as CLOSED 🏁" and then keep running in the same session indefinitely.

### Repro

1. Start a session (any platform; reproduced on Telegram DM).
2. Have a long technical back-and-forth.
3. Tell the agent explicitly the task is done ("ok this task is complete, no need to work on it any longer, consider task closed").
4. Observe: the agent acknowledges closure in its reply text, but the session object itself is untouched — `expiry_finalized: false`, `suspended: false`, no reset event logged.
5. Continue sending unrelated messages to the same chat over the following days. The session keeps accumulating real context (confirmed via `agent.turn_context: Preflight compression: ~N tokens >= threshold` log lines showing organic growth from ~70K to ~135K tokens over 4 days) and keeps re-compressing on every threshold crossing.
6. Each compression pass summarizes an already-compressed prior summary. Over ~15 compounding cycles across 4 days, the summarizer began fabricating plausible-but-untraceable technical content unrelated to any real prior request (in our case: a fictitious Chrome extension spec, drone-fleet M2M radio provisioning, private-5G cert rotation — none of which the user ever asked about), formatted convincingly as a `[CONTEXT COMPACTION — REFERENCE ONLY]` "Historical Task Snapshot," and the agent then began treating that fabricated summary as real prior context and proposing to continue it (including generating real deploy/SSH command sequences for the user's actual production infrastructure, though `tool_turns=0` on every turn in our case, so nothing was actually executed).

### Impact

- Confusing/alarming for the user: a session that repeatedly "hallucinates" specific infrastructure actions (real SSH targets, real deploy scripts, fabricated Vault-secret-fetch commands) reads exactly like a prompt-injection attack when it's actually compounding summarization drift on an abandoned thread. We initially triaged this as a likely security incident before finding `tool_turns=0` throughout the session in the logs.
- `session_reset: mode: idle` (opt-in) mitigates this once discovered, but it's not discoverable from the conversation itself — the agent's own "Task acknowledged and marked as CLOSED" response gives false confidence that something structural happened.

### Suggested fix direction

Not asking for the default to change back (the July 2026 change to `mode: none` was presumably intentional and reasonable). Instead:
1. When the agent's own response contains a task-closure acknowledgment (or, more robustly, when a lightweight classifier/heuristic detects the user declaring the task done), surface a status line or quick-reply suggesting `/reset` — something like the existing `notify` mechanism used for auto-reset, but agent-initiated rather than timer-initiated.
2. Alternatively: expose the current session's idle/age state to the agent itself as ambient context (it already knows `history=N`), so it can proactively suggest `/reset` when a long-idle, semantically-closed session receives a new unrelated message — rather than silently continuing to build on a resurrected, possibly-drifted context.

### Related known issues (found via search, likely share root cause in the reset-policy subsystem, but distinct symptom)

- #62785 — Kanban wake events defeat `session_reset` policy (sessions become immortal). Our gateway runs an active kanban dispatcher (`interval=60.0s`), so this may compound the above even with `session_reset` now opted in.
- #66255 — DB session recovery bypasses the reset policy and re-arms the idle clock.
- #67781 — Daily 4AM `session_reset` resurrected by stale-route recovery (platform/telegram).
- #43008 — idle-expiry silently starts a blank session, agent unaware it lost context (opposite failure mode, same subsystem).

None of the above cover the *conversational-acknowledgment-has-no-structural-effect* gap specifically, which is why this is filed separately.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.19.1 (2026.7.30), upstream `4e698cd4` (was 172 commits behind `origin/main` at time of report)
- Platform: Telegram DM gateway
- Model/provider during the drift: `qwen3.6:35b` via custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint (vLLM)

items.title: Context compaction after tool loop leaves stale '[memory]' as response template — all subsequent replies return '[memory]'

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
---

## Bug Description

After a context compaction event, if the agent was in the middle of a tool-call loop (specifically repeated `skill_manage` failures due to description length validation), the compaction output leaves a stale `[memory]` string that becomes the default response for **all subsequent user messages** in the conversation.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Agent enters a tool loop (e.g., 4+ retries of `skill_manage(action="create")` due to description >60 chars validation)
2. During the loop, an empty/standalone `[memory]` string is produced as a response (possibly from a tool call output being misinterpreted)
3. User sends a message — agent response gets interrupted
4. Context compaction occurs (Hermes compacts the conversation history)
5. After compaction, **every** subsequent user message receives `[memory]` as the reply instead of normal content

## Observed Behavior

- User messages: `？`, `回复这个什么意思？`, `哪里有问题？`, WeChat article link
- All received identical response: `[memory]`
- This is NOT a normal memory injection — it appears in the assistant's reply text, not in the system prompt context block
- Restarting `hermes-gateway` did not fix it (the stale state is in the session DB / compaction output)

## Evidence from Session

Session: `20260804_084359_fd07dbc0`

```
id=87753 role=assistant content="[memory]"          ← first occurrence during skill_manage loop failure
id=87755 role=user content="？"                      ← interrupted response
id=87757 role=user content="回复这个什么意思？"       ← still [memory]
id=87758 role=assistant content="[memory]"            ← NOT normal tool output, just the string
id=87759 role=user content="哪里有问题？"              ← still [memory]
id=87760 role=assistant content="[memory]"            ← same pattern continues
```

The compaction summary block (id=87689) is properly formatted as `[CONTEXT COMPACTION — REFERENCE ONLY]`. But subsequent assistant replies are just the literal string `[memory]`.

## Expected Behavior

After context compaction, the agent should continue responding normally to user messages, using the compaction summary as background context.

## Actual Behavior

All responses after compaction are the literal string `[memory]`.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent version: v0.20.0 (2026.8.3)
- Platform: Telegram
- Model: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-uncensored-heretic-Native-MTP-Preserved-Q8_0.gguf
- Provider: custom (llama-cockpit-server, port 8080)

---

items.title: [Bug]: OpenViking autostart inherits PYTHONPATH, locks Hermes venv DLLs and blocks updates

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
### Bug Description

When Hermes autostarts the OpenViking server via subprocess.Popen in `_start_local_openviking_server()` (`plugins/memory/openviking/__init__.py` line ~1229), the child process inherits the parent's PYTHONPATH, which points to hermes-agent/venv/Lib/site-packages.

This causes two cascading problems:

**Problem 1: Import pollution** - The OV process imports packages from the Hermes venv instead of its own ov-venv, because PYTHONPATH takes priority over venv site-packages. OV loads aiohttp DLLs from Hermes venv.

**Problem 2: DLL locking blocks hermes update** - On Windows, loaded DLLs are locked. When Hermes rebuilds venv during update, it fails: Cannot delete mask.cp311-win_amd64.pyd - access denied. The update aborts.

### Steps to Reproduce

Install OpenViking in a separate venv (e.g., ~/.hermes/ov-venv)
Add ov-venv/Scripts to PATH so shutil.which("openviking-server") finds it
Configure Hermes to use OpenViking as memory provider
Start Hermes desktop: the plugin autostarts OV via Popen (inheriting PYTHONPATH)
Attempt hermes update: fails with access denied on .pyd files

### Expected Behavior

Hermes update should succeed: the venv should be recreated without file access errors. The OV process should load packages from its own ov-venv, not the Hermes venv.

### Actual Behavior

Hermes update fails at the venv stage: Cannot delete aiohttp/_websocket/mask.cp311-win_amd64.pyd - access denied. Update aborts. Occurred on 2026-07-21, 2026-07-31, and 2026-08-04. Killing openviking-server allows update to succeed.

### Affected Component

Setup / Installation

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
Debug Report: Report https://paste.rs/r4Oxm
```

### Operating System

windows 10

### Python Version

_No response_

### Hermes Version

0.20.0

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
2026-08-04T02:12:19.741037Z INFO -> Creating virtual environment with Python 3.11... stage=venv 2026-08-04T02:12:19.745486Z INFO -> Virtual environment already exists, recreating... stage=venv 2026-08-04T02:12:19.829850Z INFO: Cannot delete item ...aiohttp/_websocket/mask.cp311-win_amd64.pyd: Access denied. stage=venv 2026-08-04T02:12:19.849277Z ERROR bootstrap FAILED stage=Some("venv") access denied Same error on 2026-07-21 and 2026-07-31. Killing openviking-server allows update to succeed.
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

_start_local_openviking_server() at line ~1229 uses subprocess.Popen without env=. The child inherits PYTHONPATH. Python resolves PYTHONPATH before venv site-packages, so OV imports aiohttp from Hermes venv. On Windows, loaded .pyd DLLs are locked, blocking venv recreation.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Pass a sanitized environment:
env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k != "PYTHONPATH"}
subprocess.Popen(..., env=env)

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: [Bug]: Slow startup on Windows PowerShell in corporate network (~30s delay during state.db initialization)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
### Bug Description

Starting Hermes via PowerShell on Windows in a corporate network is very slow. The startup takes significantly longer than expected, with a ~31 second gap between MCP server registration and SQLite state.db initialization.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Install Hermes on a Windows machine in a corporate network environment
2. Open PowerShell (pwsh)
3. Run `hermes`
4. Observe the startup logs — there is a ~31 second delay between MCP tool registration and state.db WAL check

### Expected Behavior

Hermes should start within a few seconds, similar to startup times on home networks or non-Windows environments.

### Actual Behavior

The following log shows the startup timeline. Note the ~31 second gap between `11:36:24,755` (MCP registered) and `11:36:55,668` (state.db WAL check):

```
2026-08-04 11:36:20,450 INFO hermes_cli.plugins: Plugin 'web-tavily' registered web provider: tavily
2026-08-04 11:36:20,452 INFO hermes_cli.plugins: Plugin 'web-xai' registered web provider: xai
2026-08-04 11:36:20,473 INFO hermes_cli.plugins: Plugin discovery complete: 55 found, 48 enabled
2026-08-04 11:36:24,754 INFO tools.mcp_tool: MCP server 'remoteshell' (stdio): registered 10 tool(s)
2026-08-04 11:36:24,755 INFO tools.mcp_tool: MCP: registered 10 tool(s) from 1 server(s)
2026-08-04 11:36:24,755 INFO tools.mcp_tool:   MCP: 10 tool(s) from 1 server(s)
2026-08-04 11:36:55,668 WARNING hermes_state: state.db: linked SQLite 3.50.4 is vulnerable to the WAL-reset corruption bug (https://sqlite.org/wal.html#walresetbug)
2026-08-04 11:36:55,724 WARNING hermes_state: state.db (async_delegation): linked SQLite 3.50.4 is vulnerable to the WAL-reset corruption bug
2026-08-04 11:36:55,795 WARNING tools.registry: check_fn check_bfl_requirements returned False; dependent tools will be unavailable this turn
2026-08-04 11:36:55,914 WARNING tools.registry: check_fn _browser_cdp_check returned False; dependent tools will be unavailable this turn
2026-08-04 11:36:55,935 WARNING tools.registry: check_fn _browser_dialog_check returned False; dependent tools will be unavailable this turn
```

The ~31s delay occurs between MCP registration and the first state.db access. This suggests the bottleneck is either:
- Opening/connecting to the SQLite database (file I/O, possibly antivirus scanning)
- Network-related delays (corporate proxy/firewall intercepting local file access, or network home directory)
- The MCP server `remoteshell` (stdio) taking time to fully initialize before control returns

### Affected Component

- CLI (interactive chat)
- Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

- N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

`hermes debug share` failed to upload — the paste service is blocked by the corporate network firewall. Unable to share debug report from the affected machine. Can provide the local output from `hermes debug share --local` manually if needed, but outbound paste service connections are blocked by the corporate proxy.

### Operating System

Windows (corporate network environment)

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

The gap between MCP registration (`11:36:24`) and state.db access (`11:36:55`) suggests the delay happens during `hermes_state` initialization. On Windows in corporate networks, common culprits include:

1. **Antivirus/EDR scanning** — corporate security tools scan newly opened files, causing multi-second delays on SQLite database access
2. **Network-redirected HOME** — if `$HOME` or `$USERPROFILE` points to a network share, SQLite WAL-mode journal I/O goes over the network
3. **Proxy interception** — corporate TLS-inspection proxies may interfere with any outgoing connections during startup (e.g., plugin/MCP health checks, update checks)

Adding timing instrumentation to the startup path (especially around `hermes_state.py` init and the gap between MCP and state.db) would help pinpoint the exact bottleneck.

items.title: Desktop: allow sessions to be manually marked unread

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Problem

Hermes Desktop can automatically mark a background session unread when its turn finishes, but a user cannot manually return a session to the unread state from the sidebar.

A common workflow is to open a completed session, realise it needs attention later, and deliberately mark it unread as a reminder. Today, opening the session clears its green indicator with no way to restore it.

## Expected behaviour

The session actions menu should expose the inverse of the existing/read-state work:

- A read session offers **Mark as unread**.
- An unread session offers **Mark as read**.
- Manually marking a session unread uses the same indicator and source of truth as automatically completed-unread sessions.
- Opening or explicitly marking the session read clears the indicator according to the established focused-session policy.

## Why this belongs in Desktop core

The existing unread state and sidebar row menu are private Desktop implementation details, not Desktop Plugin SDK contribution surfaces. A plugin cannot currently modify the built-in session menu or write `$unreadFinishedSessionIds` through a supported host action.

This is also general session-list behaviour rather than an integration-specific action.

## Related work

- #65109 introduced the automatic completed-unread indicator and is merged.
- #74162 addresses focused tile semantics for setting and clearing unread state.
- #74293 adds durable, profile-scoped unread persistence. Its current head already exposes `markSessionUnreadFinished(storedSessionId)`, which may provide the appropriate durable write path or be generalised to `markSessionUnread`.
- #76504 adds **Mark as read** and **Mark all as read** actions, but not the inverse action. It also has unresolved review feedback around tile focus policy.

This request is adjacent to those contributions and should build on their surviving state model rather than introduce another unread store.

## Acceptance criteria

- A read session can be marked unread from its sidebar actions menu.
- An unread session can be marked read from the same menu.
- The existing green unread indicator is used.
- The action is keyed by the durable, profile-scoped session identity.
- Manual unread state survives Desktop restart once the durable unread model is present.
- Opening/focusing the session clears unread consistently with the final tile-focus policy.
- Behavioural tests cover mark unread, mark read, profile scoping and restart persistence.

items.title: Gateway writes through a corrupt state.db indefinitely: one-shot FTS rebuild reports success without verifying the write path, then the 200-cap pending queue silently rotates transcripts away

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
**Not a duplicate of:** #72046 (Desktop-facing degraded-state UX + guided offline recovery — this report is the headless/gateway runtime semantics that issue explicitly scopes out) or #69603 (root cause of one re-corruption cascade — this report is about what the recovery path does *after* the rebuild fails to stick, regardless of why the file is damaged).

## Summary

When damage to `state.db` is not confined to the FTS shadow tables, the runtime recovery introduced in #66256 fails in a way that converts a detectable outage into unbounded silent data loss. In a long-running headless gateway deployment on a bind-mounted filesystem, this continued for 6 days — `append_message` failed thousands of times at WARNING level, and roughly a day of transcripts was permanently lost before a human noticed.

## Mechanism (current `main`)

1. A transcript write fails with the corrupt/malformed class. `SessionDB._try_runtime_fts_rebuild` (`hermes_state.py` ~2637) runs `rebuild_fts()` — FTS5 `'rebuild'` into the same damaged file. `rebuild_fts` (`hermes_state_search.py` ~2129) returns a count of indexes it issued the command for; any nonzero count is logged as "state.db FTS indexes rebuilt in place (N); retrying the failed write" — **success is claimed without verifying the retried write**. When the damage is B-tree/freelist rather than FTS-only, the retry fails again immediately (the exact signature quoted in #69603).
2. The one-shot flags (`_fts_runtime_rebuild_attempted`, and `SessionStore._fts_rebuild_attempted` in `gateway/session.py`) are now burned for the process lifetime, so no further recovery is ever attempted while the process keeps accepting writes.
3. Every subsequent append lands in `_dirty_transcripts` (`gateway/session.py` `_append_to_transcript_serialized`, ~3125). At `_MAX_PENDING_PER_SESSION = 200` the queue **drops the oldest message with only a WARNING** (~3141). Bounded memory, unbounded data loss.
4. The full repair ladder (`repair_state_db_schema`) only runs at open time, so a long-running gateway can never heal; nothing surfaces the condition — no ERROR-level escalation, no persistent health state, no counter. `hermes doctor` would catch it, but only if an operator already suspects a problem.

#72680 fixed the *shutdown* half of this (pending messages now spool to a JSON recovery snapshot via `flush_pending_to_file`); the *runtime* half — cap rotation while the process stays up — still loses data with no durable trace.

## Expected behavior

- A "successful" in-place rebuild whose retried write still fails should be treated as recovery failure, not success.
- Confirmed unrecoverable corruption should promote the store to a persistent degraded state (in-memory-only failure state was already ruled a bug in #74136), logged at ERROR and visible via the same surfaces that expose session-DB init failures.
- While degraded, messages that would be dropped at the pending cap should be spooled through the existing `flush_pending_to_file` recovery-snapshot path instead of discarded.
- Optionally, take one content-addressed backup of the corrupt file before further mutation attempts, mirroring the kanban DB guard's quarantine idiom (`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py:_backup_corrupt_db`) — kanban already has exactly this protection; state.db, which holds far more valuable data, does not.

I'm deliberately *not* proposing automatic failover to a fresh database: canonical rows are usually recoverable, and the project's recovery philosophy (least-destructive ladder, `hermes sessions recover` never auto-installing) argues against destructive automation. The ask is narrower: verify recovery actually worked, fail loud and durable when it didn't.

**Environment:** long-running headless gateway, Linux, bind-mounted filesystem, current `main` at time of writing.

Related: #66256, #72046, #69603, #72680, #50502, #63386, #71629, #74136.

items.title: Feature: support api_mode=responses for OpenAI Responses API protocol

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## What

Add `api_mode: responses` support so custom OpenAI-compatible providers can use the `/responses` endpoint (OpenAI Responses API), in addition to the existing `chat_completions` and `anthropic_messages` modes.

## Why

The OpenAI Responses API (`/responses`) is increasingly available on third-party endpoints alongside the traditional `/v1/chat/completions`. It has a different request/response shape:

- Input is `input` (array of content blocks) instead of `messages`
- Reasoning is `reasoning: {effort: "..."}` (structured block) instead of top-level `reasoning_effort` string
- Supports `reasoning.summary`, `store`, and other fields

Users who run multiple AI agents benefit from using the same protocol across agents, simplifying provider configuration and debugging.

## Where

Key files that would need changes:

- `agent/transports/` — new or extended transport for the Responses API payload format
- `hermes_cli/model_setup_flows.py` — add `responses` as a third choice in the api_mode selection
- `plugins/model-providers/custom/__init__.py` — extend `build_api_kwargs_extras` for Responses API reasoning format

## Current behavior

Setting `model.api_mode: responses` in config.yaml is silently ignored; the runtime falls back to `chat_completions`.

## Additional note

In `agent/transports/chat_completions.py` lines 76-82, GPT-5.6 models with `ultra` reasoning effort have it silently clamped to `max`. For providers that explicitly declare `ultra` support, this clamp may prevent users from accessing the full range of supported reasoning levels.

items.title: [Bug] v0.20.0 install/auto-update still broken: exclude-newer filters freshly pinned pillow 12.3.0 & setuptools 83.0.0 (build-system fails too)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #75992: the `exclude-newer = "14 days"` setting in `pyproject.toml` (`[tool.uv]`) still breaks installs and auto-updates on the **released v0.20.0 (2026.8.3)**, and now fails at *build* time — not just dependency resolution. The project pins exact versions that were published within the last 14 days, uv filters them out, and resolution can never succeed until the pins age out of the window.

## Environment

- macOS (arm64)
- Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (2026.8.3), install method: git
- Python 3.11.15, uv 0.6.13

## Error 1 — runtime dependency (`pillow==12.3.0`)

```
× No solution found when resolving dependencies:
╰─▶ Because there is no version of pillow==12.3.0 and hermes-agent==0.20.0 depends on pillow==12.3.0, we can conclude that
    hermes-agent==0.20.0 cannot be used.
    And because only hermes-agent==0.20.0 is available and you require hermes-agent, we can conclude that your requirements are
    unsatisfiable.

hint: `pillow` was filtered by `exclude-newer` to only include packages uploaded before 2026-07-21T03:58:37.027941Z. Consider using `exclude-newer-package` to override the cutoff for this package.
```

## Error 2 — build dependency (`setuptools==83.0.0`) — this is new and worse

```
warning: setuptools-80.10.2-py3-none-any.whl is missing an upload date, but user provided: 2026-07-21T05:42:17.100653Z
warning: setuptools-81.0.0.tar.gz is missing an upload date, but user provided: 2026-07-21T05:42:17.100653Z
warning: setuptools-81.0.0-py3-none-any.whl is missing an upload date, but user provided: 2026-07-21T05:42:17.100653Z
warning: setuptools-82.0.0.tar.gz is missing an upload date, but user provided: 2026-07-21T05:42:17.100653Z
warning: setuptools-82.0.0-py3-none-any.whl is missing an upload date, but user provided: 2026-07-21T05:42:17.100653Z
warning: setuptools-82.0.1.tar.gz is missing an upload date, but user provided: 2026-07-21T05:42:17.100653Z
warning: setuptools-82.0.1-py3-none-any.whl is missing an upload date, but user pr
  × Failed to build `hermes-agent @ file:///Users/lw/.hermes/hermes-agent`
  ├─▶ Failed to resolve requirements from `build-system.requires`
  ├─▶ No solution found when resolving: `setuptools==83.0.0`
  ╰─▶ Because there is no version of setuptools==83.0.0 and you require
      setuptools==83.0.0, we can conclude that your requirements are
      unsatisfiable.

hint: `setuptools` was filtered by `exclude-newer` to only include packages uploaded before 2026-07-21T05:42:17.112469Z. Consider using `exclude-newer-package` to override the cutoff for this package.
✗ Could not auto-recover the interrupted install.
```

Note the second failure is in `build-system.requires`: the package **cannot even be built** from a git checkout right now. The 14-day filter applies to build-time requirements too, so a fresh git install of v0.20.0 is impossible until the pinned `setuptools==83.0.0` ages out.

## Impact

- Every git-install auto-update (0.19.1 → 0.20.0) currently fails, leaving the same `.update-incomplete` marker described in #75992; startup recovery hits the same wall.
- Because the cutoff is relative (`now − 14 days`), this is a rolling trap: **any** dependency the project pins that was released in the last fortnight breaks the install. It already hit `pillow`, `setuptools`, and per #75992 `mcp` — and will keep recurring.
- Manual recovery works but is not obvious to end users.

## Request

Please prioritize a fix — e.g. merge #76020 (or equivalent) that exempts the project's own pinned packages (`pillow`, `setuptools`, `mcp`) via `exclude-newer-package`, and ideally exclude `build-system.requires` from the snapshot cutoff entirely so a project can always build itself. v0.20.0 shipped with a broken upgrade path for git installs; users are stuck on 0.19.1 (or failing updates) in the meantime.

## Workaround for affected users

```bash
cd /path/to/hermes-agent
uv pip install -e '.[all]' --exclude-newer-package pillow --exclude-newer-package setuptools
# or bypass uv entirely:
venv/bin/python -m pip install -e '.[all]'
```

items.title: User message re-injected mid-turn hours after original delivery (duplicate OUT-OF-BAND message)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Summary
A user message that was delivered and processed at 13:08 was injected AGAIN as a mid-turn (OUT-OF-BAND) message at 14:05, hours later, with identical content. The user did not send a second message.

## Evidence
- **state.db (messages table)**: only ONE user message with this content exists (timestamp 13:08). No second user message at 14:05.
- **gateway.log**: only one inbound message with this content at 13:08. Between 14:00-14:06 only two unrelated inbound messages were logged (a different user request and the user's follow-up asking about the issue).
- **Agent received**: a mid-turn OUT-OF-BAND message at ~14:05 whose content is byte-identical to the 13:08 message.
- The agent treated it as a new instruction and re-ran the previously completed operation (idempotent, so no damage, but potentially dangerous for non-idempotent commands).

## Environment
- Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (git main, 2026-08-04)
- Windows, gateway mode (Feishu platform)
- Happened while the agent was mid-turn running a long background task

## Expected
Mid-turn user message injection should only deliver genuinely new user messages. Already-delivered/processed messages should never be re-injected, especially hours after the original.

## Impact
If a historical message containing a destructive or non-idempotent instruction were replayed this way, the agent would execute it a second time without the user asking.

items.title: Windows local terminal sessions cannot access configured SMB drive mappings

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
## Problem

On Windows, mapped network-drive letters are scoped to a logon/session token. A Hermes gateway or background process can therefore create a local terminal environment that cannot see mappings available in Explorer or another interactive process.

This prevents terminal commands from accessing UNC-backed workspaces even when Windows Credential Manager already has valid credentials.

## Proposed behavior

Add opt-in `terminal.windows_network_drives`. When Hermes creates a local terminal environment on Windows, it should remove a stale mapping, map each configured UNC path with `net use <drive>: <unc> /persistent:no`, rely on Windows Credential Manager rather than storing credentials, and log failures without blocking startup.

## Scope

Only the local Windows terminal backend; disabled by default. No model tool or host-specific configuration is added.

items.title: [Bug]: hermes version silently reports "Up to date" on shallow installs — CLI drops the -1 no-count sentinel that the desktop already handles

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Summary

`hermes version` (and the startup banner) can never announce an update on a **shallow git install** (`git clone --depth 1` — the standard installer path). When upstream moves, the check returns the `UPDATE_AVAILABLE_NO_COUNT` sentinel (`-1`) and the CLI's print logic has no branch for it, so it prints **nothing** — and after the 6h cache was written while current, it prints the actively wrong **"Up to date"**. The desktop app already solves this exact case; the CLI path does not.

## Environment

- **OS:** Linux / WSL2 / macOS (any — this is git-logic, not platform)
- **Install method:** git, shallow (`git clone --depth 1`)
- **Hermes version:** v0.20.0 (upstream 743dc94ab)

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
# 1. Fresh install is shallow:
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent.git
cd hermes-agent
hermes version            # → "Up to date" (true only for the first minutes)

# 2. Upstream pushes. Wait >6h (or rm ~/.hermes/.update_check), then:
hermes version            # → prints NOTHING after "OpenAI SDK: 2.24.0"
                          #    (the -1 sentinel falls through both branches)
git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/main   # → e.g. 11  (we ARE behind)
```

Observed: either a stale cached **"Up to date"** (when the 6h cache was written while current) or **complete silence** (when the cache expires and the fetch detects the drift — returns `-1`, which `cmd_version` drops).

Expected: `Update available: N commits behind — run 'hermes update'` (when countable) or at minimum `Update available — run 'hermes update'` (when the count isn't meaningful).

## Root cause

Two pieces that disagree:

1. `hermes_cli/banner.py` — `check_for_updates()` returns `UPDATE_AVAILABLE_NO_COUNT = -1` for shallow checkouts (no merge-base to count against, deliberate — counting across the boundary reports a bogus "12492 commits behind"). The docstring even says the sentinel exists so callers can show "an update exists but count unknown".

2. `hermes_cli/main.py` — `_print_version_info()` only handles:
   ```python
   if behind and behind > 0:   # prints "Update available: N commits"
   elif behind == 0:           # prints "Up to date"
   ```
   `-1` matches neither → **silent**. Combined with the 6h `.update_check` cache, the user most often sees the cached `0` ("Up to date") even while 11+ commits behind.

## The fix already exists in the codebase

The desktop update indicator solved the identical shallow case in `apps/desktop/electron/update-count.ts`:

```ts
// Resolve how many commits the local checkout is behind origin
// When the count isn't meaningful (shallow + no merge-base):
return 1 // behind by an unknown amount — show a generic "update available"
```

The CLI should mirror that contract: handle `UPDATE_AVAILABLE_NO_COUNT` by printing a generic "Update available — run 'hermes update'" (without a count), instead of falling through to silence. Local repro patch (25 lines, tested):

```diff
-        from hermes_cli.banner import check_for_updates
+        from hermes_cli.banner import UPDATE_AVAILABLE_NO_COUNT, check_for_updates
         from hermes_cli.config import recommended_update_command
 
         behind = check_for_updates()
         if behind and behind > 0:
             commits_word = "commit" if behind == 1 else "commits"
             print(
                 f"Update available: {behind} {commits_word} behind — "
                 f"run '{recommended_update_command()}'"
             )
+        elif behind == UPDATE_AVAILABLE_NO_COUNT:
+            print(
+                "Update available (shallow checkout — commit count unknown) — "
+                f"run '{recommended_update_command()}'"
+            )
         elif behind == 0:
             print("Up to date")
```

## Related issues (cache/staleness — distinct root causes, same symptom family)

- #23681 — update check cache hides commit list until manually deleted
- #11327 — banner shows stale "commits behind" after successful update (cache not invalidated)
- #40944 — banner shows stale count after manual `git pull` in source installs
- #72789 — update banner silently blind on fork-based deployments (different cause: fork origin URL path)
- #45556 — local audit note: stale update cache can show false behind count

This issue is the **shallow-clone sentinel** slice: the check *knows* an update exists but cannot count it, and the CLI drops that knowledge entirely.
